title: The Agents Howard Lutnick Pulled off Their Jobs
zh_title: 特工霍华德·卢特尼克完成了他们的工作
summary: 商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克在上任之初就疏远了他的常规安全人员，其中一些人辞职了。他不必四处寻找替代者。商务部自己的工业和安全局雇用携带武器并有权逮捕人员的执法人员。该部门重新指派其中一些人担任卢特尼克的私人保镖，从而摆脱了原本可以阻止人工智能芯片走私到中国的特工职责。相反，他们现在会乘坐他的私人飞机旅行并守卫他的各个住所，
content:
商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克在上任之初就疏远了他的常规安全人员，其中一些人辞职了。他不必四处寻找替代者。商务部自己的工业和安全局雇用携带武器并有权逮捕人员的执法人员。该部门重新指派其中一些人担任卢特尼克的私人保镖，从而摆脱了原本可以阻止人工智能芯片走私到中国的特工职责。据五位知情人士透露，他们现在将乘坐他的私人飞机出行并看守他的各个住所。一些商务官员对卢特尼克为了保护自己而转移人员感到困惑，因为美国正竞相在先进人工智能领域保持领先于中国。国际清算银行是美国执行出口管制的主要机构，其代理人接受过培训，以防止美国珍贵技术落入坏人之手。从理论上讲，他们应该站在阻止非法人工智能芯片交易的最前线——这是围绕英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋及其与涉嫌中国间谍的关系引发争议的核心问题。 （黄承认了此事，但​​表示他不知道该女子可能是中国间谍。）BIS 特工接受过执法许多方面的培训，包括犯罪现场调查和反恐。
然而，他们没有接受过保护贵宾和政要的培训。商务部有自己的安全办公室，至少从 1986 年起就向秘书提供保护。但这种保护传统上比为更密切参与国家安全的高级官员提供的保护要轻，后者被认为更有可能成为目标。前官员告诉我们，任命 BIS 特工担任保镖似乎是因为卢特尼克希望获得与国防部长和司法部长等其他内阁成员相当的细节。民主党人和一些共和党人质疑为什么卢特尼克没有采取更多措施来阻止英伟达和其他公司非法销售先进芯片，或者扩大以国家安全为由禁止进行此类采购的公司名单。特别是，立法者希望更多地了解 Lutnick 对 Megaspeed 的处理方式，Megaspeed 是一家总部位于新加坡的公司，因潜在的芯片走私而受到美国商务部和司法部的调查。即使大约一年前，美国情报部门认定 Megaspeed 高管 Alice Huang 为中国情报资产，并与黄仁勋有恋爱关系，商务部也没有将 Megaspeed 列入贸易黑名单。
该公司昨天才被列入名单，就在同一天，英伟达董事会在特朗普总统的压力下恢复了黄仁勋担任公司总裁和首席执行官的职务。然而，迟来的列入黑名单似乎更具象征意义，而不是实质性的：一位贸易专家表示，由于将 Megaspeed 添加到名单中的法规的编写方式，该公司仍然可以获得多种类型的人工智能芯片。工业安全局只有不到200名特工；他们中的大多数人在美国各地的 10 个办事处工作，还有大约十几个在海外工作。目前尚不清楚有多少特工受到卢特尼克保护人员轮换的影响。二

【原文 English Original】
E arly in his tenure , Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick so alienated members of his regular security detail that some of them quit. He didn’t have to look far for replacements. The Department of Commerce’s own Bureau of Industry and Security employs law-enforcement agents who carry weapons and have the power to arrest people. The department reassigned some of them to serve as Lutnick’s personal bodyguards, pulling away from their duties agents who might otherwise have prevented the smuggling of AI chips to China. Instead, they would now travel on his private jet and guard his various homes, according to five people with knowledge of the matter. Some commerce officials were baffled that Lutnick had diverted personnel for his own protection as the United States is racing to stay ahead of China on advanced artificial intelligence. BIS is the nation’s leading bureau for the enforcement of export controls, and its agents are trained to keep prized U.S. technology out of the wrong hands. In theory, they should be on the front lines of the effort to prevent illicit AI-chip trading—the issue at the center of the controversy over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his relationship with an alleged Chinese spy. (Huang has admitted to the affair but said that he hadn’t known that the woman might have been a Chinese spy.) BIS agents are trained in many aspects of law enforcement, including crime-scene investigation and counterterrorism. They are not, however, trained in protecting VIPs and dignitaries. The Commerce Department has its own Office of Security, and secretaries have been provided with protection since at least 1986. But that protection has traditionally been lighter than what’s provided to senior officials who are more closely involved in national security, who are considered more likely targets. The assignment of BIS agents as bodyguards, former officials told us, seemed driven by Lutnick’s desire to have a detail comparable to that of other Cabinet members, such as the secretary of defense and the attorney general. Democrats and some Republicans have questioned why Lutnick hasn’t done more to prevent illegal sales of advanced chips from Nvidia and other firms, or expanded the list of companies that are barred on national-security grounds from making such purchases. In particular, lawmakers want to know more about Lutnick’s approach to Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that’s under investigation by Commerce and the Justice Department for potential chip smuggling. Even after U.S. intelligence, about a year ago, identified the Megaspeed executive Alice Huang as a Chinese-intelligence asset who was in a romantic relationship with Jensen Huang, the Commerce Department didn’t put Megaspeed on its trade blacklist. The company was added only yesterday, the same day that Nvidia’s board restored Jensen Huang to his roles as the company’s president and chief executive, under pressure from President Trump. The belated addition to the blacklist appears to have been more symbolic than substantive, however: One trade expert suggested that because of the way the regulation adding Megaspeed to the list was written, the company would still have access to many types of AI chips. T he Bureau of Industry and Security has fewer than 200 special agents; most of them work in 10 field offices across the United States, and about a dozen or so work overseas. It wasn’t clear how many agents were affected by the rotations onto and off Lutnick’s protection staff. Two former officials told us that the assignment usually involved three to four agents at a time. A Commerce Department official said in a statement that “at a time when the Secretary was facing the highest level of credible threats in the Department’s history some agents were temporarily detailed to augment executive protection.” The official added that the number of agents at BIS has increased, though she didn’t provide numbers. As artificial intelligence has boomed, the bureau has struggled to keep pace with the global trade in U.S. chips, suggesting that it could ill-afford the secondment of agents elsewhere. The Commerce Department’s Office of the Inspector General, in a June report, found that BIS has not taken adequate action to enforce export controls on goods destined for China and Hong Kong. In a report a month earlier, it found similar enforcement failures regarding Russia and Belarus. [ Read: The limits of positive thinking ] Overall, the number of public penalties and enforcement actions for violating U.S.-export rules has fallen since Lutnick took office in February 2025. Across 2023 and 2024, the annual case rate was close to 100; in the 17 months from March 2025 to the start of August, the annualized rate dropped to about half that, according to The Export Practitioner , a trade publication. Amid the furor over Nvidia, the inspector general last week began an evaluation of the bureau’s oversight of advanced-computing chips. Current and former commerce officials we spoke with put the blame for the bureau’s lackluster performance on Lutnick and his team. They contend that Lutnick and senior officials have repeatedly stressed Trump’s interest in a détente with China and have placed commercial interests above national security. Trump has made clear his desire for a new China trade deal and last week sought to further improve relations with President Xi Jinping at a summit in Shenzhen . Trump’s approach runs counter to the administration’s aggressive posturing about the need to restrict Chinese trade. The diversion of agents to serve in Lutnick’s protective detail has sapped expert resources and prevented agents from doing the high-stakes work they are hired and trained to perform, current and former officials told us. “They’re not trained for protective detail,” one current official told us. “These are professional investigators.” A former official called it “completely inappropriate” to pull agents to protect Lutnick. The Commerce Department, meanwhile, is seeking an increase in staffing. In April, Lutnick told the House Appropriations Subcommittee that BIS needed additional resources and enforcement personnel, including 290 new enforcement officers, to prevent the diversion of semiconductors to China and to protect American innovation. He didn’t mention the redeployment of some of the officers whom BIS already employed. L utnick , a friend of Trump’s and a former Wall Street executive, is one of the Cabinet’s wealthiest members. His most recent financial-disclosure form lists his holdings, which include a $25 million mansion that he purchased in 2024 in the Berkley neighborhood of Washington, D.C. The house, modeled after France’s Château du Grand-Lucé, was until recently the most expensive home ever sold in the capital. Lutnick also owns properties in New York City, the Hamptons, and South Florida. He made much of his money as the CEO of Cantor Fitzgerald, a New York financial firm, where his two sons, Brandon and Kyle, hold senior leadership positions. Cantor also held approximately 1.8 million Nvidia shares as of the end of June, which were valued at the time at $362 million, according to the company’s financial disclosures. (The firm has said that it has no material proprietary position in Nvidia, and its holdings mainly arise from its services for clients.) [ Read: The president’s most annoying buddy ] Lutnick no longer has a financial interest in Cantor Fitzgerald, but some in Congress have argued that his close family ties to the firm represent a conflict of interest. Some White House officials have privately expressed similar worries, according to several current and former administration officials. Despite these concerns, and Lutnick’s well-documented feuds with others at the top of the administration, Trump has consistently rebuffed pushes to drop his friend from the Cabinet. Jack Rodriquez-Vars contributed to this report.

title: In Pictures: Hundreds gather for Catholic memorial mass on eve of Tai Po fire’s first anniversary
zh_title: 图片中：大埔火灾一周年前夕，数百人聚集参加天主教纪念弥撒
summary: 去年大埔致命火灾一周年纪念日前夕，数百人聚集在一起举行天主教弥撒，一名神父称这次仪式是与幸存者的陪伴，并宣读了 168 名遇难者的名字以示悼念。 2026 年 11 月 25 日，一场天主教弥撒纪念大埔火灾受害者。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。天主教香港教区周三晚上在中环圣母无染原罪主教座堂举行了追悼弥撒，有200多名死者家属参加。所有168名遇难者的名字都被展示在了现场
content:
去年大埔致命火灾一周年纪念日前夕，数百人聚集在一起举行天主教弥撒，一名神父称这次仪式是与幸存者的陪伴，并宣读了 168 名遇难者的名字以示悼念。 2026 年 11 月 25 日，一场天主教弥撒纪念大埔火灾受害者。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。天主教香港教区周三晚上在中环圣母无染原罪主教座堂举行了追悼弥撒，有200多名死者家属参加。所有 168 名遇难者的名字都陈列在圣所的中央，下面还放着一些遇难者的肖像。他们的名字也印在数字礼拜仪式小册子上。 2026 年 11 月 25 日，一场天主教弥撒纪念大埔火灾受害者。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。主持仪式的陈华明神父在讲道中表示，这场致命的大火是一次集体创伤，幸存者、他们的家人和公众都遭受了巨大的痛苦和悲伤。陈用粤语说：“追悼会聚集了分散的、独自悲伤的人们，让他们意识到他们并不孤单面对这一切。” 2026 年 11 月 25 日，一场天主教弥撒纪念大埔火灾受害者。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。
他还将这场悲剧描述为源于“人为错误和系统性故障”，这与一个独立委员会的调查结果相呼应，该调查将装修承包商和项目顾问列为“罪魁祸首”，并强调了政府监管的失误。“这项服务提醒我们，人的生命不是可随意处置的数字，而是来自上帝的珍贵礼物，”他说。 “这种对生命的坚韧应该转化为对真理和正义的追求。” 2026 年 11 月 25 日，一场天主教弥撒纪念大埔火灾受害者。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。香港福音派信义会钻石堂牧师林珍妮在火灾中失去了三名亲戚，她也在弥撒中发表了讲话，当天恰逢她一位已故亲戚的生日。 “但我不能再亲自祝他们生日快乐了，”她用粤语说。林郑月娥表示，过去的一年对死者家属来说充满了挑战，并列举了葬礼安排方面的繁重行政职责以及悲剧造成的情感损失。 2026 年 11 月 25 日，一场天主教弥撒纪念大埔火灾受害者。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。她说，虽然时间并没有减轻痛苦，但她祈祷家人能够过上好日子，并保留对亲人的记忆。她补充说，这并不意味着忘记受害者，而是从创伤中治愈，同时为悲伤留出空间。
四名失去亲人的幸存者大声朗读了 168 名遇难者的名字，最后是在与大火搏斗中牺牲的消防员何伟豪。2026 年 11 月 25 日，一场天主教弥撒悼念大埔火灾遇难者。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 2026 年 11 月 25 日，一场天主教弥撒纪念大埔火灾受害者。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。宏福苑宏新楼居民大聪在葬礼结束后告诉记者，当受害者的名字被大声念出来时，她感到很安慰，并补充说，死者家属承受着无法用言语形容的痛苦。在大火中失去母亲的菲利斯·罗(Phyllis Lo)表示，当她听到母亲的名字时，她感到很平静，并想象着其他受害者的名字被读出时的生活。 2026 年 11 月 25 日，一场天主教弥撒纪念大埔火灾遇难者。

【原文 English Original】
Hundreds gathered on the eve of the first anniversary of last year’s deadly Tai Po fire for a Catholic mass, where a priest described the service as an act of companionship with survivors and the names of the 168 people who perished were read out in tribute. A Catholic mass remembering Tai Po fire victims on November 25, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The Catholic Diocese of Hong Kong held the memorial mass on Wednesday evening at the Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception in Central, with members of bereaved families among more than 200 attendees. The names of all 168 victims were displayed at the centre of the sanctuary, with portraits of some placed underneath. Their names were also printed in digital liturgy booklets. A Catholic mass remembering Tai Po fire victims on November 25, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Father Dominic Chan, who presided over the service, said during his homily that the deadly blaze was a collective trauma, and that survivors, their families and members of the public all suffered immense pain and grief. “The memorial mass brings together scattered people who grieve on their own, to make them realise that they are not alone in facing this,” Chan said in Cantonese. A Catholic mass remembering Tai Po fire victims on November 25, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. He also described the tragedy as one stemming from “human errors and systemic failures,” echoing an independent committee’s findings that named a renovation contractor and project consultant as the “main culprits” and highlighted lapses in government oversight. “This service reminds us that human lives are not disposable numbers, but cherished gifts from God,” he said. “This tenacity for life should be transformed into a pursuit for truth and justice.” A Catholic mass remembering Tai Po fire victims on November 25, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Jenny Lam, a pastor at the Diamond Church of the Evangelical Lutheran Church of Hong Kong who lost three relatives in the fire, also spoke during the mass, which coincided with the birthday of one of her late relatives. “But I can no longer wish them happy birthday in person,” she said in Cantonese. The past year had been full of challenges for bereaved families, Lam said, citing the enormous administrative duties surrounding funeral arrangements alongside the emotional toll of the tragedy. A Catholic mass remembering Tai Po fire victims on November 25, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. While time had not dulled the pain, she said, she prayed that families would be able to live well and keep alive the memories of their loved ones. That did not mean forgetting the victims, but healing from the trauma while allowing room for grief, she added. The names of the 168 victims were read aloud by four bereaved survivors, ending with Ho Wai-ho, a firefighter who died in the line of duty battling the blaze. A Catholic mass remembering Tai Po fire victims on November 25, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. A Catholic mass remembering Tai Po fire victims on November 25, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Da Chung, a resident of Wang Fuk Court’s Wang Sun House, told reporters after the service that she felt solace as the victims’ names were read aloud, adding that bereaved families carry pain that words cannot describe. Phyllis Lo, who lost her mother in the blaze, said she felt calm when she heard her mother’s name, and imagined the lives of the other victims as their names were read out. A Catholic mass remembering Tai Po fire victims on November 25, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Wednesday’s mass was overshadowed by controversy surrounding police enquiries into memorial events related to the Tai Po fire earlier this month. One church, the Immaculate Heart of Mary Church in Tai Po , has since replaced its anniversary mass with a general service for “the brothers and sisters who died in the past year.” A Catholic mass remembering Tai Po fire victims on November 25, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Parishioners have criticised authorities for exerting pressure, but security chief Chris Tang has defended the move , saying it was necessary for authorities to assess risks for public events. A Catholic mass remembering Tai Po fire victims on November 25, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Agnes Ng, a Catholic who lost her mother in the blaze, told HKFP on Wednesday that she had helped organise the mass while residing overseas. She struck a defiant note when asked whether she perceived pressure from the authorities. A Catholic mass remembering Tai Po fire victims on November 25, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “They were being oversensitive… The fire occurred in Tai Po, and the Tai Po church was the most appropriate venue for a memorial service,” she said in Cantonese. “If police ask me, I will welcome them.” “[The blaze] is not just a Wang Fuk Court matter. It relates to all Hongkongers,” she added. “It’s sensible, lawful and reasonable for us to hold a mass to honour the dead. Why do we have to self-censor?”

title: 蘇暁康：下一個「民族寓言」誰來寫？
summary: 作者臉書 2026-11-25 【按：深圳的光鮮亮麗，以及它從一個小漁村暴漲至今的發跡史，都是一個「中國敘述史」的簡略版本，它亮麗得太短，因為中國人又懷念起魯迅了，說明她還在「前現代」和農民大國掙扎，也沒有逃出「民族預言」的詛咒，諸如「吃人」、溺婴、婴儿汤、吃药、「中国病毒」⋯⋯。】 一、崛起：全球政治菁英的整體失敗 二〇一九年底，在国际视野里的最大新闻，却是“中国崛起”，其最初信号来自两本英文周刊。 封面上章子怡笑容可掬，背后衬着万里长城和上海东方明珠塔，两件中国的标志性
content: 作者臉書 2026-11-25 【按：深圳的光鮮亮麗，以及它從一個小漁村暴漲至今的發跡史，都是一個「中國敘述史」的簡略版本，它亮麗得太短，因為中國人又懷念起魯迅了，說明她還在「前現代」和農民大國掙扎，也沒有逃出「民族預言」的詛咒，諸如「吃人」、溺婴、婴儿汤、吃药、「中国病毒」⋯⋯。】 一、崛起：全球政治菁英的整體失敗 二〇一九年底，在国际视野里的最大新闻，却是“中国崛起”，其最初信号来自两本英文周刊。 封面上章子怡笑容可掬，背后衬着万里长城和上海东方明珠塔，两件中国的标志性建筑。2005年5月初，最新一期美国《新闻周刊》推出封面故事：中国的世纪 (china’s century )，用21个版面进行密集报道，从商业、教育、电影等多个角度解读当今中国，它明确阐释就是：中国的崛起已不再是预测，而是事实。但是这个特别报道是留有余地的，以“未来是否属于中国？”为总题，因为崛起的含义，只在经济层面。 比如，中国激活世界经济。数字表明，中国一切都很大，有13亿人口，是世界最大的煤、钢铁和水泥生产国，是世界第二大能源消费国和第三大石油进口国，这样一个经济体，为全世界带来了明显和惊人的利益，特别是对于美国，廉价的中国产品，在上个世纪使美国消费者节省了超过6000亿美元，更有一种分析认为，中国经济的强劲增长，使全世界经济免于萧条。 过去四百年年中，全球强权有两个主要变化，第一个是17世纪欧洲的兴起，第二个是19世纪末、20世纪初美国的独大，现在中国与印度的兴起以及日本的持续发展，代表了亚洲的崛起，这是不是意味着欧洲和美国衰落了呢？ https://www.facebook.com/xiaokang.su/posts/10157925323368331 二、從崛起到坍塌 2012年中国正在崛起，难道是比拟纳粹的崛起吗？ 89则是对中共很不祥的数字，自然直指它的执政危机。 但是有人分析： ——中国根本就不可能出希特勒，眼下到处都腐败，就更不可能，出了也让老百姓把他赶下去； ——中国出现的专制，肯定是土的，水平低的，是中国专制主义加一点现代化； ——这个土的，不会是“Hi，希特勒”，也不会是“伟大领袖毛主席万岁”； 显然，有看走眼的成分，也有惊人的准确；其二，似乎曾在中国横行的毛泽东统治，死了几千万人，不叫专制，这是遗忘呢，还是虚无？ 更重要的是第三，还有改革开放吗？改革死了吗？尤其2018年岁尾中共煞有介事高调纪念改革开放40周年，一种“伪改革”还冠冕堂皇地活在主流话语中，企业家、知名党内外知识份子，仍在谈“改革经”。 https://www.facebook.com/xiaokang.su/posts/10161000344588331 三、今天中国的「民族寓言」是什么？ 我过去以为今天的年輕人不認識魯迅，如今網上每每見人喜歡引用名句（現在叫「金句」），是不是魯迅的引用率最高？當然因為魯迅最深刻，不過我覺得恐怕也是他最刻薄——當下人們恨中共恨中國恨習，自然最喜歡最刻薄的名句，像胡適那種不帶火氣的溫吞句是無人理睬的，可能也被引用得最少。不過大夥兒可能忘了，喜歡引用名人名句恰是一種「失語」現象，因為自己忽然有了某種比較深刻的想法，卻一時欠缺用自己的語詞表達出來，看到某個名句正好暢快淋灕地表達了自己想說的，馬上拿來引用。 不过，知道毛澤東的「靈魂深處爆發革命」，源頭在鲁迅那裡的人可能不多。中國因為落後而需要改造人的思想，就跟得病需要吃藥一樣，這是魯迅發明的一種「五四」傳統，最終成為共產黨的一把利器，中宣部及其黨報電視台，至今使喚它得心應手，他們不懂什么「劣等人種」，只有「病人」概念，中国人至今還是阿Q、閏土、華老栓，一代代人都要服药（改造）。 今天人们依然叹服魯迅骂中国人「坐稳了奴隶」的深刻，可是无人询问今天的「民族寓言」是什么？中国不「吃人」了吗？溺婴、婴儿汤算什么？中国人不是还在吃药吗？中国开发病毒「泄漏」到全球，跟当年英国人贩鸦片到中国，是一种因果关系？「大国崛起」的原动力来自当年的「亡国灭种」，这可能是一部新的「民族寓言」？ https://www.facebook.com/xiaokang.su/posts/10160793058903331 https://vocus.cc/article/6b0659edfd89780001cfafb4... vocus.cc APEC鎂光燈外看深圳

title: Sicilian chef Angelo Agliano brings simple philosophy to Hong Kong fine dining
zh_title: 西西里主厨 Angelo Agliano 将简约哲学带入香港美食
summary: 西西里主厨 Angelo Agliano 为香港美食带来简约理念 |中国劳工布告栏 星期五, 2026 年 11 月 27 日 · 香港 香港及中国劳工英文新闻 西西里厨师 Angelo Agliano 为香港美食带来简单哲学 香港丽思卡尔顿酒店米其林一星 Tosca di Angelo 餐厅的总监 Angelo Agliano 厨师分享了他的简约烹饪哲学。他讲述了他从西西里岛到香港的旅程、为足球明星做饭以及获得米其林三颗星的梦想。主厨 Angelo Agliano，米其林一星餐厅 Tosca di Angelo 的总监
content:
西西里主厨 Angelo Agliano 为香港美食带来简约理念 |中国劳工公告栏
星期五, 27 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
西西里主厨 Angelo Agliano 将简约哲学带入香港美食
香港丽思卡尔顿酒店米其林一星 Tosca di Angelo 餐厅的总监、主厨 Angelo Agliano 分享了他简约的烹饪哲学。他讲述了他从西西里岛到香港的旅程、为足球明星做饭以及获得米其林三颗星的梦想。
香港丽思卡尔顿酒店米其林一星 Tosca di Angelo 餐厅的总监、主厨 Angelo Agliano 认为，简单是最难掌握的菜肴。 “做一道简单的菜比做一道复杂的菜要困难得多。有了简单，就没有隐藏在装饰品后面的东西，”他说。他的理念在世界意大利美食周的大师班上得到了体现，他教学生用西西里红虾和罗勒香蒜酱烹饪 mezzi paccheri。
阿利亚诺今年 50 岁，在厨房工作了 30 年。他的职业生涯包括为足球明星克里斯蒂亚诺·罗纳尔多做饭，但他最自豪的球迷时刻是前国际米兰队长哈维尔·萨内蒂参观他的餐厅。 “我的父亲和我都是哈维尔·萨内蒂的超级粉丝，”他说。 “然后有一天，我发现他在餐厅吃午饭。”在台北的六年里，他与华语流行巨星王力宏建立了一段不可思议的友谊，这促使他学习普通话。 “2010年，台湾几乎没有人说英语。所以我强迫自己学习，”他说。
他的季节性菜单每三个月更换一次，他说这种纪律可以让“你的幻想、你的激情”保持活力。他大量使用当地农产品，尤其是香港的海鲜。 “这里的石斑鱼太棒了，比欧洲好得多。在欧洲……太难了。这里的鱼仍然很小，而且很嫩，”他说。他住在大角咀，经常去当地的菜市场，不仅去餐厅，还在家做饭。
他对鸡肉划清界限。 “香港的黄鸡太美味了。它属于自己的。我的菜单上从来没有它，”他说。他还对不起眼的月饼情有独钟，这要归功于他的中国厨师自制的月饼。 “我总是告诉他，这是我一生中[我尝试过的]最好的。顶，顶，顶，顶，”他说。
阿利亚诺的香港之旅从来没有计划过。他被法国厨师 Joël Robuchon 从蒙特卡洛挖来，帮助在香港和台北开设了 L'Atelier de Joël Robuchon，并在香港特别行政区任职期间获得了米其林三颗星。在台湾度过了一段安静的时光后——“我觉得很无聊”，他承认——2016 年回到台湾，开设了自己的餐厅，然后才担任目前的职务，因为他渴望这座城市的“独特的电力”。他将香港的餐饮业与东京、纽约、巴黎和伦敦进行了比较：“如果你做得不好，你就出去。”
他有一个明确的梦想：开一家刻有他名字的米其林三星级餐厅。但他并不是为了自我而追星。 “当你获得这样的奖项时，你真的很高兴。但对我来说，这是关于激情。幻想。保持它的活力，”他说。对于那些认为意大利菜以披萨开始和结束的人来说，他微笑了。 “当然，我们提供精致的美食。但是当你品尝到完美的菜肴时——糖、盐、一点脂肪，一切都很均衡——每一口[让你发现]一个不同的水平。然后当你吃完后，你会想再去一次。”

Friday, 27 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Sicilian chef Angelo Agliano brings simple philosophy to Hong Kong fine dining
Chef Angelo Agliano, director of one-Michelin-star Tosca di Angelo at The Ritz-Carlton, Hong Kong, shares his culinary philosophy of simplicity. He discusses his journey from Sicily to Hong Kong, cooking for football stars, and his dream of earning three Michelin stars.
Chef Angelo Agliano, director of one-Michelin-star Tosca di Angelo at The Ritz-Carlton, Hong Kong, believes simplicity is the hardest dish to master. "Doing a simple dish is much more difficult than doing a complicated one. With simplicity, there is no hiding behind ornaments," he said. His philosophy was on display during masterclasses for the Week of Italian Cuisine in the World, where he taught students to cook mezzi paccheri with Sicilian red shrimps and basil pesto.
Agliano, 50, has spent 30 years in the kitchen. His career includes cooking for football star Cristiano Ronaldo, but his proudest fan moment came when former Inter Milan captain Javier Zanetti visited his restaurant. "My father and I were huge fans of Javier Zanetti," he said. "Then one day, I find him in the restaurant for lunch." During six years in Taipei, he struck up an unlikely friendship with Mandopop superstar Wang Leehom, which pushed him to learn Mandarin. "In 2010, almost no people spoke English in Taiwan. So I forced myself to learn," he said.
His seasonal menus change every three months, a discipline he said keeps "your fantasy, your passion" alive. He draws heavily on local produce, particularly Hong Kong's seafood. "The grouper here is amazing, much better than Europe. In Europe it's … too hard. Here the fish is still small and very tender," he said. He lives in Tai Kok Tsui and visits the local wet market regularly, not just for the restaurant but for cooking at home.
He draws the line at chicken. "Hong Kong's yellow chicken is too nice. It belongs on its own. I never have it on my menu," he said. He also has a soft spot for the humble mooncake, thanks to his Chinese chef's homemade version. "I tell him always, it's the best [I've ever tried] in my life. Top, top, top, top," he said.
Agliano's journey to Hong Kong was never planned. Plucked from Monte Carlo by French chef Joël Robuchon, he helped open L'Atelier de Joël Robuchon in Hong Kong and Taipei, earning three Michelin stars during his tenure in the SAR. After a quieter stint in Taiwan – "I got boring," he admits – he returned in 2016 and opened his own restaurant before taking on his current role, craving the city's "unique electricity." He compared Hong Kong's dining scene to Tokyo, New York, Paris, and London: "If you're not good, you go out."
He has a clear dream: a three-Michelin-star restaurant with his name on it. But he is not chasing stars for ego. "When you get to this kind of award, you're really happy. But for me, it's about the passion. The fantasy. Keep it alive," he said. To anyone who thinks Italian food begins and ends with pizza, he smiled. "Of course, we do fine dining. But when you taste the perfect dish – sugar, salt, a bit of fat, all balanced – every bite [makes you discover] a different level. Then when you finish, you want to go again."

梁志强荣获工总奖年度工业家奖 |中国劳工公告栏
星期五, 27 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
梁志强荣获香港工业总会年度工业家奖
梁君源荣获香港工业总会颁发年度工业家奖。四位青年领袖还因其在金属、眼镜、纺织和智能能源领域的工作而荣获青年工业家奖。
2026 年 11 月 26 日 23:15 香港时间 · 更新于 11 月 27 日 04:25 · 阅读时间 1 分钟
香港工业总会（工总）于11月26日星期四举行颁奖典礼，颁发2026年香港青年工业家奖及年度工业家奖。
新兴针织厂顾问、前立法会主席梁君源获颁年度工业家奖。 50多年来，梁振英倡导跨境产业联系、清洁生产和职业教育。他还帮助成立了香港知专设计学院和香港高等教育科技学院，并支持中小企业的研发和融资。
梁振英在接受这一荣誉时赞扬先辈们引导工业从自动化和“前店后厂”合作发展到今天的新型工业化，并称工业是香港经济的基石。
四位领导者荣获金属、眼镜、纺织和智能能源领域的香港青年工业家奖。他们分别是南星金属制品有限公司执行董事康家明、OKIA Optical董事总经理林志豪、Tessellation Group品牌及零售总裁潘楚英，以及Halo Energy行政总裁曾伟华。他们的工作涵盖一站式金属解决方案、可持续眼镜、无水染色和智能电动汽车充电。
工总主席林世豪向所有得奖者表示祝贺，并勉励业界为下一代开拓新机遇，推动新型工业化。

Andrew Leung named Industrialist of the Year at FHKI awards | China Labour Bulletin Board
Friday, 27 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Andrew Leung named Industrialist of the Year at FHKI awards
Andrew Leung Kwan-yuen received the Industrialist of the Year Award from the Federation of Hong Kong Industries. Four young leaders were also honoured with Young Industrialist Awards for work in metals, eyewear, textiles and smart energy.
26 Nov 2026 at 23:15 HKT · updated 27 Nov, 04:25 · 1 min read
The Federation of Hong Kong Industries (FHKI) presented the 2026 Young Industrialist Awards of Hong Kong and the Industrialist of the Year Award at a ceremony on Thursday 26 November.
Andrew Leung Kwan-yuen, a consultant at Sun Hing Knitting Factory and former president of the Legislative Council, received the Industrialist of the Year Award. Over more than 50 years, Leung championed cross-border industrial ties, cleaner production and vocational education. He also helped establish the Hong Kong Design Institute and the Technological and Higher Education Institute of Hong Kong, and supported research and development and financing for small and medium-sized enterprises.
Accepting the honour, Leung credited earlier generations for guiding industry from automation and “front shop, back factory” collaboration to today’s new industrialisation, calling industry the bedrock of Hong Kong’s economy.
Four leaders earned Young Industrialist Awards of Hong Kong across metals, eyewear, textiles and smart energy. They are executive director Gordon Hong of South Star Metal Products, managing director Jacky Lam Chi-ho of OKIA Optical, president of brands and retailing Dee Poon Chu-ying of Tessellation Group, and chief executive Martin Tsang Wai-wah of Halo Energy. Their work spans one-stop metal solutions, sustainable eyewear, water-free dyeing and smart electric-vehicle charging.
FHKI chairman Anthony Lam Sai-ho congratulated all the winners and urged the industry to open up new opportunities for the next generation and to drive new industrialisation.

summary: 下载整期 PDF 作为全球台湾研究所致力于促进声音多元化的一部分，全球台湾简报偶尔会发表台湾年轻人撰写的文章。我们很高兴以一名高中生的视角来阐述年轻人在复杂的互联网信息环境中所面临的挑战，以及台湾学校关于公民教育的持续争论。台湾面临着一些严重的威胁，不仅来自直接的军事力量，还来自我在同龄人中经常看到的自我挫败的态度。虽然在国外
content:
下载整期 PDF 作为全球台湾研究所致力于促进声音多元化的一部分，全球台湾简报偶尔会发表台湾年轻人撰写的文章。我们很高兴以一名高中生的视角来阐述年轻人在复杂的互联网信息环境中所面临的挑战，以及台湾学校关于公民教育的持续争论。台湾面临着一些严重的威胁，不仅来自直接的军事力量，还来自我在同龄人中经常看到的自我挫败的态度。尽管外国观察家警告两岸可能发生冲突，但年轻人流行的社交媒体平台上却充斥着“战争不会爆发”、“台湾无论如何也不会赢”或“谁统治我们并不重要”等言论。但这些言论并不代表台湾大多数青年群体的声音，也不应被视为整个一代人放弃的证据。然而，随着对民主的冷漠成为日常谈话的一部分，它产生了一种值得关注的脆弱性。问题的出现并不仅仅是因为一些学生对政治了解太少。事实上，我们许多人在与我们学校设计的环境截然不同的信息环境中遭遇政治。公民教育仍然主要通过教科书、考试和课堂讲座进行。
然而，政治叙事现在通过短视频、影响者、模因和推荐算法传达给我们。如果学校以中立的名义避免讨论有争议的问题，学生将不会变得政治中立：相反，他们会去其他地方学习政治。当政治通过信息传播时 中国社交媒体平台已成为台湾信息环境的主要组成部分。 TikTok、抖音和 Rednote 等平台模糊了娱乐和政治影响力之间的界限。事实上，可能影响台湾人的内容并不总是需要采用明显的宣传。现代天际线、高铁、传统文化、美食、乡村生活、普通家庭的视频都能让中国成为一个熟悉而有吸引力的国家。政治信息可以通过娱乐视频传播，而台湾年轻人可能根本不认为这些是政治信息。这不是一个边缘问题。事实上，Doublethink Lab 2025 年的一项研究（使用台湾传播调查的数据）发现，50.73% 的高中生使用 TikTok。研究人员还采访了 16 名 15 岁至 18 岁的台湾用户，发现政治视频有时会意外地出现在社交媒体群组中，尤其是在 2024 年总统选举前后。尽管如此，研究人员发现，大多数青少年仍然对中华人民共和国政府持负面看法，反对统一。
因此，声称使用中国平台会让台湾青少年“亲中国”的说法过于简单化。更重要的问题可能是台湾年轻人在这些平台上遇到什么样的政治信息，以及他们如何理解这些信息。当我们超越屏幕上出现的内容时，这种担忧变得更加清晰。 2025 年对 700 名台湾 Z 世代成员进行的一项同行评审研究发现，更频繁地使用中国社交媒体平台（包括 TikTok、Rednote 和微博）与对两岸事务的政治了解较低有关

【原文 English Original】
DOWNLOAD FULL ISSUE PDF As part of the Global Taiwan Institute’s commitment to promoting a diversity of voices, the Global Taiwan Brief occasionally publishes articles written by Taiwanese youth. We are pleased to present this perspective from a high school student about the challenges young people face in navigating a complex internet information environment, and continuing debates over civic education in Taiwan’s schools. Taiwan faces several serious threats, not only from direct military forces, but also from a self-defeating attitude that I see frequently in people of my age. While foreign observers warn of the possibility of a cross-Strait conflict, social media platforms popular among young people are filled with claims that “War won’t break out,” “Taiwan could never win anyway,” or “It doesn’t matter who governs us.” Nonetheless, these statements do not represent the voice of the majority of youth groups in Taiwan, and they should not be seen as proof that the entire generation has given up. However, as indifference toward democracy becomes a part of everyday conversation, it creates a sort of vulnerability that deserves attention. The problem arises not simply because some students know too little about politics. In fact, many of us encounter politics in an information environment very different from the one for which our schools were designed. Civic education still largely proceeds through textbooks, exams, and classroom lectures. Political narratives, however, now reach us through short videos, influencers, memes, and recommendation algorithms. If schools avoid discussing controversial issues in the name of neutrality, students will not become politically neutral: instead, they will go somewhere else to learn about politics. When Politics Spreads Through the Feed Chinese social media platforms have become a major part of Taiwan’s information environment. Platforms such as TikTok, Douyin, and Rednote blur the line between entertainment and political influence. Indeed, content that may impact Taiwanese does not always have to employ obvious propaganda. Videos of modern skylines , high-speed rail, traditional culture, food, rural life, or ordinary families can render China a familiar and attractive country. Political messages can then spread through entertainment videos, and Taiwanese youth may not perceive these as political messages at all. This is not a marginal issue. In fact, a 2025 Doublethink Lab study —using data from the Taiwan Communication Survey—found that 50.73 percent of high-school students used TikTok. Researchers also interviewed sixteen Taiwanese users aged fifteen to eighteen and discovered that political videos had sometimes appeared unexpectedly in social media groups, especially around the 2024 presidential election. Nonetheless, the researchers found that most of these teenagers still had negative views of the PRC government and opposed unification. It is thus an oversimplification to claim that using Chinese platforms makes Taiwanese teenagers “pro-China.” The more important question may be what kind of political information Taiwanese youth encounter on those platforms, and how they understand it. That concern becomes clearer when we look beyond what appears on the screen. A 2025 peer-reviewed study of 700 members of Taiwan’s Generation Z found that more frequent use of Chinese social media platforms—including TikTok, Rednote, and Weibo—was associated with lower political knowledge about cross-Strait affairs, and a weaker ability to tell the different usages of language between China and Taiwan. Greater use of Chinese social media was also linked to a decreased ability to identify People’s Republic of China (PRC) disinformation. This does not necessarily mean that young people are being “brainwashed.” The problem may be more subtle. If people have less knowledge about an issue, it becomes harder for them to judge whether the information they see is reliable in the first place. The numbers from another Doublethink Lab nationwide survey make this picture even more complicated. Among 2,612 Taiwanese respondents aged fifteen and above, the majority of both frequent and non-frequent TikTok users rejected the idea of giving up democracy for cross-Strait peace. Yet there was still a difference between the frequent and non-frequent users. The study found that 30.3 percent of frequent users were willing to accept giving up democracy for peace, compared with 23.4 percent of non-frequent users. Frequent users were also more likely to believe that unification with China might not significantly change everyday life in Taiwan. These numbers do not prove that TikTok caused these attitudes. But they do suggest that cognitive influence does not have to make young Taiwanese actively admire Beijing. Sometimes, it may simply make the differences between democratic and authoritarian systems feel less important, or make resistance seem less worthwhile. What “Politics Out of Schools” Originally Meant If political influence increasingly reaches students through their phones, then Taiwan must also ask what role schools should play. Here, our democratic history creates an ironic situation. During the authoritarian period of Taiwan, politics was not absent from Taiwanese campuses. Rather, politics was deeply intertwined with education. Historical records show that Kuomintang (國民黨) organizations, the China Youth Corps (中國青年救國團), military instructors, and state security agencies were involved in monitoring and managing university campuses. In 1986 and 1987, as Taiwan moved toward democratization, students involved in the “Freedom of Love” movement (自由之愛運動) at National Taiwan University demanded freedom of speech, university autonomy, and reform of the University Act (大學法) , as well as the removal of party organizations, the Youth Corps, and military instructors from campuses. This history matters because the original democratic demand was not that students should stop discussing politics. Instead, it was that the party-state should stop controlling political life in schools. Indeed, demands for political institutions to leave campuses appeared alongside demands for greater freedom of expression. Removing political control is not the same as removing political discussion. Taiwan’s legal framework still reflects this distinction. Article 6 of the Educational Fundamental Act (教育基本法) requires education to follow a principle of neutrality and prohibits schools from either campaigning for particular political organizations, or forcing teachers and students to participate in political activities. The restriction is directed at the institution, not at the student. Taiwan democratized its schools by making institutions politically neutral, not by requiring students to be politically silent. Image: A teacher and students at Baozhong Junior High School in Yunlin County, Taiwan (December 2019). Image source: Wikimedia Commons ) From Political Neutrality to Political Silence Yet in practice, the memory of authoritarian political indoctrination may have encouraged a broader habit of avoiding controversial politics in school. The idea that “politics should not enter schools” (政治不入校園) can be interpreted not only as a warning against party control, but also as a reason for teachers to avoid politically sensitive issues. This is different from the original purpose of educational neutrality, which was to protect students from forced ideology, rather than to stop them from discussing political life. The same tension can also be seen inside schools. A National Academy for Educational Research (國家教育研究院) survey of high-school history teachers found broad support for teaching transitional justice, but more than 60 percent of teachers worried that such teaching could be influenced by partisan viewpoints. Among teachers who did not design additional lessons on transitional justice, fear of being accused of partisan indoctrination was the second most common reason— after lack of class time. This does not mean that teachers do not want to discuss politics. Rather, it shows how easily civic education can be confused with political indoctrination, even in a democratic society. The tension is especially clear because Taiwan’s curriculum has moved in the opposite direction. The 108 Curriculum (108課綱) included transitional justice in high-school history, and education researchers have also recommended using multiple historical perspectives to encourage discussion and reflection. Formally, schools are therefore expected to help students think critically about history, understand different perspectives, and reflect on democratic values. At the same time, teachers may still worry about being accused of taking sides. As many of my classmates have noticed, political issues can therefore become exam facts that we memorize for answer sheets, but quickly escape our memory. Civics exists as an academic subject, but politics does not always become part of students’ real lives. History can feel distant from our own identities, while democratic rights become background conditions that we assume will always exist. When students then hear “If there’s war, just surrender” or “It doesn’t matter who is in charge,” they may understand the danger of war without having seriously thought about what political change could mean for freedom of speech, elections, personal rights, or the rule of law. This is where the role of the classroom becomes important. Schools should not tell students which party to support or what position to take on cross-Strait relations. Instead, they should give students a place to ask questions, test claims, compare evidence, and discuss difficult issues. Research using data from 3,953 Taiwanese students in the International Civic and Citizenship Education Study found that an open classroom climate for discussion was associated with stronger civic knowledge and expected electoral participation. In other words, students do not become better citizens simply because disagreement is kept out of the classroom. They need opportunities to learn how to disagree while still respecting evidence, rights, and one another. Rebuilding Civic Resilience Taiwan can learn from the experiences of other democracies. Austria has included political education in its formal education system and emphasizes that controversial issues should also be presented as controversial in the classroom, while avoiding political indoctrination. Finland , meanwhile, treats media literacy as an important part of education and integrates it across subjects, helping students understand information, media, and misleading content. These two examples show that political education and media literacy do not have to mean telling students what to believe. Instead, they can help students understand political issues, recognize different viewpoints, and evaluate the information they receive. Taiwan has also begun to recognize this need. In 2025, the Ministry of Education (教育部) announced plans to develop teaching materials on understanding China, including cross-Strait relations, national identity, and possible risks. By July 2025 , thirteen teaching materials had undergone initial review, and were still being revised and supplemented. However, as a student on the front line of Taiwan’s education system, I was barely aware of this plan. Most of the teachers and classmates I asked had not heard about it either. Even if the material is still under review, students should be able to understand what is being prepared, why it is needed, and when they may actually have the chance to use it. A policy cannot have much effect on students if the students themselves barely possess awareness of it. For this reason, the Taiwanese government should expedite the development of these materials and simultaneously seek to raise awareness among students and teachers regarding what changes are underway. However, teaching materials alone may not be enough. Taiwan should also consider adding more opportunities for civic education and discussion in schools, especially on topics such as cross-Strait relations, democracy, media literacy, and how political information affects our daily lives. Taiwan does not need to copy either Austria or Finland’s models exactly. Its own history provides the more important lesson. Taiwan’s democratization movement fought to remove one-party control from schools so that thought could become freer. The purpose of that effort was never to create classrooms in which politics could not be discussed. Modern cognitive warfare makes this distinction urgent. Algorithms do not respect the principle of “politics out of schools.” They enter teenagers’ lives every day, deciding what we see. If schools in democracies respond by remaining silent, they leave the most politically consequential part of students’ education to systems designed not to educate citizens, but to maximize attention. The challenge, then, is not to bring partisan politics back into schools. It is to bring democratic politics back into civic education. Students should understand how Taiwan’s freedoms were won, how authoritarian systems differ from democratic ones, how algorithms can shape political perception, and how to examine claims without automatically accepting or rejecting them because of party labels. Taiwan’s psychological defense will not be built by teaching young people what to think. It will be built by giving them the knowledge and habits necessary to decide what is worth defending for themselves. The main point: As political information increasingly reaches Taiwanese youth through social media, schools’ reluctance to discuss controversial issues may leave students more vulnerable to misleading narratives and cognitive influence. Political neutrality should not mean political silence. Instead, Taiwan’s civic education should encourage open discussion, critical thinking, and media literacy, allowing students to develop their own informed judgments about democracy and the challenges it faces. The post Observations from Taiwan’s Education Frontline amid Cognitive Warfare appeared first on Global Taiwan Institute .

The Death of Logic and Sanity in Silicon Valley bbert@hudson.org Tue, 11/24/2026 - 13:49 SVG Commentary Nov 24, 2026 Washington Times The Death of Logic and Sanity in Silicon Valley Our technology giants are helping China challenge American supremacy   Miles Yu Senior Fellow and Director, China Center Miles Yu Commentary Caption The headquarters of NVIDIA in the Silicon Valley, Santa Clara, California, November 6, 2025. (Getty Images) Toggle Table of Contents Contents Contents Share to Twitter Twitter Share to Facebook Facebook Share to LinkedIn LinkedIn Share to E-mail E-mail Print Print Something has gone terribly wrong in Silicon Valley . The industry that made America the world’s technological superpower has produced executives whose commercial ambitions increasingly collide with national security. Their dealings with communist China expose an astonishing paradox: American technology companies help China catch up with the United States, then warn that China is catching up, and finally use that warning to demand permission to sell China even more advanced technology. No one is more vocal in advancing this lunacy than Nvidia’s now-reinstated CEO Jensen Huang . Mr. Huang’s latest scandal has been sensationalized, focusing on his illicit relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese national and a former executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed . Yet the bigger issue is Mr. Huang’s absurd ideas about China and its artificial intelligence industry. Mr. Huang has repeatedly argued that China is catching up with or even winning the AI race, that American export controls are futile or “the dumbest thing we’ve ever done” and that restricting advanced chip sales to China will ultimately undermine American technological leadership. He says those resisting his ideas — whom he labels “ China hawks” — are unpatriotic and un-American. These arguments are intellectually vacuous, characteristically arrogant, strategically reckless and remarkably self-seeking for Nvidia’s commercial interests. Worse, they reflect a broader Silicon Valley mentality that confuses corporate profits with America’s national interest. Consider the contradictions. If China is winning the AI race, why are Chinese companies so desperate for Nvidia’s advanced chips? If American AI models such as Claude and ChatGPT are losing their technological edge, why do China’s top AI firms, such as Kimi and Alibaba, seek to extract their capabilities through large-scale distillation? If American export controls are futile, why does Beijing devote extraordinary resources to circumventing them? How can supplying America’s foremost strategic adversary with the technologies underpinning American supremacy possibly strengthen America’s competitive advantage? Mr. Huang’s vicious dismissal of “ China hawks” as wearing a “badge of shame” makes defending American technological superiority sound disgraceful whenever it interferes with corporate profits. His arguments collapse under the absurdity of their own logic. In fact, this is Silicon Valley’s self-fulfilling prophecy, a circular argument that converts the consequences of its own commercial decisions into justification for repeating them. China’s technological progress remains critically dependent on American semiconductor designs, advanced AI chips, computing infrastructure and technical expertise. Without access to these capabilities, Beijing would face far greater obstacles in developing cutting-edge AI. China’s scientists and engineers are capable, and its government invests enormous resources in innovation. Yet its relentless pursuit of American technology reveals how much its technological ambitions still depend on foreign breakthroughs. Mr. Huang’s corporate behavior is also in question. Multiple reports indicate that Megaspeed has purchased more than $4.8 billion in advanced Nvidia AI chips since June 2024 and has erased the records of these transactions from its books. American authorities have investigated suspected diversion through Southeast Asian intermediaries. Reports have also raised questions about Ms. Huang’s suspected ties to Chinese intelligence. Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter reportedly contacted Commerce Department investigators, citing clearance from Undersecretary Jeffrey Kessler, regarding the Megaspeed investigation. Nvidia denies wrongdoing and says it stopped supplying Megaspeed in June 2025, but recent reports dispute the denial. Congress and law enforcement should investigate the Megaspeed affair, examine possible interference with export-control enforcement and close loopholes involving third-country intermediaries, remote computing access and sensitive technology licensing. Proven violations deserve serious penalties. Nvidia is hardly alone. Consider Advanced Micro Devices CEO Lisa Su, Mr. Huang’s distant cousin. In 2016, under her leadership, AMD entered into a technology-licensing agreement worth approximately $293 million, plus royalties, with Chinese partners affiliated with the Chinese Academy of Sciences. The arrangement transferred valuable x86-compatible processor technology and first-generation Zen intellectual property into China’s industrial ecosystem. The available record indicates the transaction was lawful. Its strategic wisdom deserves scrutiny. Why should American companies help develop China’s indigenous computing capabilities and then warn Americans about the technological challenge they helped create? Cisco provides another cautionary example. Falun Gong practitioners accused the company of supplying technologies that helped China’s Golden Shield surveillance system identify and track religious believers. Cisco disputed the allegations, and this year the U.S. Supreme Court dismissed the lawsuit, holding that the Alien Tort Statute does not allow aiding-and-abetting liability against corporations. Yet the controversy illustrates the risks of American technology becoming entangled with authoritarian surveillance. The Chinese Communist Party systematically mobilizes civilian technology for military modernization, intelligence operations and political control. U.S. executives advocating greater access to technology for China must confront these strategic consequences. America’s technological supremacy rests on decades of innovation, enormous investment and hard-won expertise. Allowing these advantages to strengthen its principal strategic adversary threatens the foundations of American security. Silicon Valley has perfected a vicious cycle of strategic folly: Sell advanced American technology to China , often knowingly and furtively through a third, surrogate country such as Singapore. Watch Beijing close the gap. Warn Americans that China is catching up. Declare export controls futile. Demand permission to sell even more advanced technology to China . Repeat. Each turn enriches Silicon Valley , strengthens Beijing and erodes America’s technological supremacy. The closer China gets, the louder the alarm — and the louder the alarm, the greater the pressure to sell China more. Eventually, the prophecy fulfills itself: Silicon Valley helps China catch up, warns America that China is catching up, and uses that warning to help China catch up even faster, until America loses the race its own technology giants helped China win. In other words, Silicon Valley has lost its mind. In explaining his support for Mr. Huang’s reinstatement, President Trump has said Mr. Huang has learned his lessons. Let us hope these lessons learned will help Silicon Valley regain its sanity. Read in the Washington Times. Enjoyed this analysis? content:
一名 37 岁的陆军后勤军士在承认参与阴谋向与中国有关的个人传输敏感国防信息后，将面临最高 10 年的监禁。美国俄勒冈州地区检察官斯科特·E·布拉德福德 (Scott E. Bradford) 周二宣布，中士。驻扎在华盛顿刘易斯-麦科德联合基地的赵健已认罪，最高刑罚包括 25 万美元罚款和 10 年监禁。官员们在美国陆军和司法部联合发布的新闻稿中表示，赵于 2017 年入伍，并保持安全许可，作为其职责的一部分，这使他能够访问敏感的军事信息和设备。一项联邦调查确定，2021 年 11 月至 2025 年 3 月期间，赵曾与包括另一名前士兵段若宇在内的团伙合作，“获取并向中国买家转让与国防相关的信息和设备。”据新闻稿称，段已承认串谋传输国防信息罪。调查人员称，他招募了赵和其他现役军人来收集和提供军事信息，并安排与中国买家的沟通和货币兑换。据新闻稿称，赵向买家提供的机密敏感信息包括高机动火炮火箭系统（HIMARS）的部分技术手册。
官员们说，他还用自己的个人手机拍摄了“有关美国陆军行动、通信网络、火箭和导弹系统以及军事演习的受限军事演示和文件”。此外，他还提出出售一些政府硬盘和计算机。官员称，3 月 6 日，联邦特工搜查了赵在华盛顿莱西的家，发现并收回了陆军硬盘、未指明的电子设备和约 3 万美元现金，赵因此被捕。作为认罪的一部分，赵交出了这笔现金，并同意另外没收 17,500 美元，被视为“犯罪所得”。他将于 2027 年 3 月 1 日被判刑。陆军反情报司令部司令肖恩·斯廷琼将军称赵的行为“故意背叛了每个士兵保卫我们国家和保护我们战友的誓言”。他在一份声明中表示：“此人通过利用敏感军事信息和政府设备来换取个人利益，破坏了我们陆军的作战安全，并使士兵面临风险。” “我敦促我们队伍中的每个人保持警惕，并向陆军反情报部门报告任何可疑活动或外展活动。”现役部队滥用敏感军事信息来援助美国对手的案例很少见，但并非闻所未闻。
2025 年，22 岁的陆军坦克兵泰勒·亚当·李 (Taylor Adam Lee) 因涉嫌试图向俄罗斯情报官员传输机密军事信息（包括操作 M1A2 艾布拉姆斯坦克的详细信息）而被捕。该案尚未进入审判阶段。 2024 年，前海军士官“托马斯”赵文衡因向一名中国情报官员发送敏感军事信息以换取贿赂而被判入联邦监狱 27 个月。美国司法部表示，这些敏感信息包括“太平洋战区的大规模海上训练演习、作战命令以及地面/空中任务东方的电气图和蓝图”。

【原文 English Original】
A 37-year-old Army supply sergeant is facing up to 10 years in prison after pleading guilty to participating in a conspiracy to transfer sensitive national defense information to China-connected individuals.  U.S. Attorney for the District of Oregon Scott E. Bradford announced Tuesday that Sgt. Jian Zhao, stationed at Joint Base Lewis-McChord, Washington, had entered the guilty plea, which carries a maximum penalty that includes a $250,000 fine as well as a decade of prison time. Zhao enlisted in the Army in 2017 and maintained a security clearance as part of his duties that gave him access to sensitive military information and equipment, officials said in a joint U.S. Army-Department of Justice release. A federal investigation determined that, between November 2021 and March 2025, Zhao had worked with a group including another former soldier, Ruoyu Duan, ” to obtain and transfer information and equipment related to the national defense to buyers in China.” Duan, according to the release, has already pleaded guilty to conspiracy to transmit national defense information. Investigators say he recruited Zhao and other active-duty troops to gather and provide military information and arranged communication and the exchange of money with buyers from China. The classified and sensitive information Zhao provided to the buyers included parts of technical manuals for the High Mobility Artillery Rocket System, or HIMARS, according to the release. He also used his personal cell phone to take pictures of “restricted military presentations and documents concerning U.S. Army operations, communications networks, rocket and missile systems and military exercises,” officials said. In addition, he offered to sell a number of government hard drives and computers. Zhao was arrested March 6 when federal agents raided his home in Lacey, Washington, finding and recovering Army hard drives, unspecified electronic devices and about $30,000 in cash, officials said. As part of his plea, Zhao surrendered that cash and agreed to forfeit an additional $17,500 considered “proceeds of the offense.” He is set to be sentenced on March 1, 2027. Brig. Gen. Sean Stinchon, commanding general of Army Counterintelligence Command, called Zhao’s actions “a deliberate betrayal of the oath every soldier takes to defend our nation and safeguard our fellow service members.” “By trading access to sensitive military information and government equipment for personal profit, this individual undermined our Army’s operational security and put soldiers at risk,” he said in a statement. “I urge everyone across our ranks to stay vigilant and report any suspicious activity or outreach to Army Counterintelligence.” Cases of active-duty troops abusing access to sensitive military information to aid U.S. adversaries are rare, but not unheard of. In 2025, 22-year-old Army tank crewman Taylor Adam Lee was arrested on allegations of trying to transmit classified military information, including details of operating the M1A2 Abrams tank, to a Russian intelligence officer. That case has not yet gone to trial. And in 2024, former Navy Petty Officer Wenheng “Thomas” Zhao received 27 months in federal prison for sending sensitive military information to a Chinese intelligence officer in exchange for bribes. The DOJ said this sensitive information included “large-scale maritime training exercise in the Pacific theatre, operational orders and electrical diagrams and blueprints for a Ground/Air Task Oriented Radar system located in Okinawa, Japan.” Another former soldier, Korbein Schultz, was sentenced to 84 months in 2025 for conspiring to collect sensitive military information, including pre-deployment operational orders, F-22 fighter jet and intercontinental ballistic missile technical manuals, and details on U.S. military exercises. He attempted to sell the information to a Chinese agent, investigators said .

content:
由于车辆许可证申请推迟，香港网约车服务推出推迟至 2027 年中国劳工公告栏
星期五, 27 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
由于车辆许可证申请推迟，香港网约车服务推出推迟至 2027 年
香港当局已将获得许可的网约车平台的推出推迟至 2027 年初，未能达到原定的年底目标。车辆许可证申请数量上限为 10,000 份，将于明年初开放，并采用投票系统，为经验丰富的驾驶员和长期车主提供额外的机会。
2026 年 11 月 27 日 02:32 香港时间 · 更新于 11 月 27 日 04:24 · 阅读时间 2 分钟
香港当局已将获得许可的叫车服务的启动时间推迟到明年初，从而将启动时间推迟到原定的 2026 年底之前。运输署署长于 11 月 27 日宣布，网约车许可证的公开邀请（上限为 10,000 个配额）要到 2027 年初才会开放，这意味着平台在今年年底前不会开始运营。
根据立法会于2025年10月通过的监管框架，第一批规定于2026年8月3日生效。首批网约车服务牌照预计将于11月底发放，平台将于第四季度投入运营。消息人士称，略微推迟的原因是，审查多达八家寻求平台许可证的组织的申请所需的时间以及尚未解决的网约车驾驶许可证和网约车许可证的技术细节。
交通官员表示，如果申请超过 10,000 份配额，许可证将以抽签方式分配。每个符合资格的申请人将至少收到一份基本参赛作品，但两组将获得额外的机会。第一组涵盖在明年初许可证申请截止日期之前通过综合笔试或已持有有效网约车驾驶许可证的申请人（包括转换执照的出租车司机）。第二组包括在 2026 年 8 月 3 日之前在指定期限内拥有私家车的个人。
当局解释说，加权抽签奖励那些尽早准备满足牌照要求的申请者，同时防止未来的司机急于购买仅用于商业运营的私家车，这可能会加剧道路拥堵。
立法会交通事务委员会主席陈汉斌支持8月3日的车辆保有量限制，指出这可以阻止突然的抢购热潮，并防止没有私家车的的士司机集体弃车参加抽签，从而扰乱现有的士运营。他敦促当局确保投票机制保持公平和透明。
中国香港汽车协会终身名誉会长李耀培表示，鉴于国际城市游客对网约车服务的强劲需求，优先考虑经验丰富的司机是合理的，并补充说经验丰富的运营商有助于稳定市场。他估计，已经拥有私家车的年轻兼职出租车司机最有可能转向网约车。

Hong Kong ride-hailing launch delayed to 2027 as vehicle permit applications postponed | China Labour Bulletin Board
Friday, 27 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong ride-hailing launch delayed to 2027 as vehicle permit applications postponed
Hong Kong authorities have pushed back the launch of licensed ride-hailing platforms to early 2027, missing the original year-end target. Vehicle permit applications, capped at 10,000, will open early next year with a ballot system giving extra odds to experienced drivers and long-term car owners.
27 Nov 2026 at 02:32 HKT · updated 27 Nov, 04:24 · 2 min read
Hong Kong authorities have delayed the start of licensed ride-hailing services until early next year, pushing back the launch beyond an original end-of-2026 target. The Commissioner for Transport announced on 27 November that public invitations for ride-hailing vehicle permits — capped at 10,000 quotas — will not open until early 2027, meaning platforms will not begin operations before the end of this year.
Under the regulatory framework passed by the Legislative Council in October 2025, the first batch of provisions took effect on 3 August 2026. Initial ride-hailing service licences had been expected to be issued by the end of November, with platforms operating in the fourth quarter. Sources cited the time needed to vet applications from up to eight organisations seeking platform licences and unresolved technical details for both ride-hailing vehicle driving permits and ride-hailing vehicle permits as reasons for the slight postponement.
Transport officials said that if applications exceed the 10,000 quota, permits will be allocated by ballot. Every eligible applicant will receive at least one basic entry, but two groups will get extra chances. The first group covers applicants who have passed the integrated written examination or already hold a valid ride-hailing vehicle driving permit — including taxi drivers converting their licences — before the permit application deadline early next year. The second group comprises individuals who have owned a private car for a designated period before 3 August 2026.
Authorities explained that the weighted ballot rewards applicants who prepare early to meet licensing requirements while preventing prospective drivers from rushing to purchase private cars solely for commercial operation, which could worsen road congestion.
Ben Chan Han-pan, chairman of the Legislative Council Panel on Transport, backed the 3 August vehicle ownership cutoff, noting it discourages a sudden buying spree and prevents taxi drivers without private cars from abandoning taxis en masse to enter the draw, which would disrupt existing taxi operations. He urged authorities to ensure the ballot mechanism remains fair and transparent.
Ringo Lee Yiu-pui, honorary life president of the Hong Kong, China Automobile Association, said granting priority to experienced drivers was reasonable given strong tourist demand for ride-hailing services in an international city, adding that seasoned operators help stabilise the market. He estimated that younger, part-time taxi drivers who already own private cars would be the most likely to transition to ride-hailing.

Chinese v American Views on WAR with Taiwan
Posted Aug 14, 2026 by Martin Armstrong |
The Center for Strategic and International Studies conducted an extraordinary survey of 64 leading experts on China, Taiwan, and cross-Strait relations, including 28 former senior U.S. government officials, 23 former government policy and intelligence analysts, and 13 academics and think-tank experts. What their answers reveal is not that China is preparing to invade Taiwan tomorrow, as the neocons would like everyone to believe, but that Beijing remains willing to wait so long as nobody crosses the line of formal Taiwanese independence. Some 84% said Beijing is willing to wait for unification but will not accept the status quo permanently, while only 10% believed China seeks unification at the earliest opportunity. Not one of the 64 experts believed Beijing would ever accept an independent Taiwan.
This is precisely why Taiwan has become so dangerous. The West keeps portraying the conflict as if Xi Jinping wakes up every morning staring at a calendar trying to decide when to launch an amphibious invasion. Yet 83% of these experts said China did not plan to use significant kinetic force against Taiwan by 2027, and 80% said China’s enormous 2022 military exercises did not indicate Beijing had accelerated its timetable. Only 6% of respondents outside the former senior government group saw 2027 as a hard deadline, while not one former senior U.S. official did. The obsession with 2027 has nevertheless become extremely useful for the military establishment because every supposed deadline becomes another justification for weapons, deployments, bases, and spending.
The survey found that 44% believed Beijing has a hard deadline of 2049, the centennial of the People’s Republic, while 42% believed China could wait indefinitely provided unification remains possible. This is an important distinction because China thinks in terms of generations while Western politicians think in terms of the next election. Beijing does not need to invade Taiwan if economic, political, and military pressure can gradually change the situation in its favor. Only 20% of those surveyed believed China even possessed a coherent roadmap for peaceful unification, which tells us this is not some perfectly scripted invasion plan sitting in Xi’s desk drawer.
Where the numbers become alarming is not an unprovoked invasion but what happens when politicians begin crossing China’s red lines. More than three-quarters of the experts, 77%, believed China would invade within six months if Taiwan formally declared independence. Among former senior U.S. officials, that number was 79%. Even some of those who did not expect an immediate invasion believed Beijing would respond with a blockade or enormous military exercises. This is why politicians encouraging Taiwan toward formal independence are playing with the lives of 23 million people. They can deliver all the speeches they want about democracy from Washington, London, or Brussels, but they will not be the civilians sitting underneath the missiles if their political experiment goes wrong.
Not one expert believed an explicit American commitment to defend Taiwan would cause China to invade immediately, but 64% believed Beijing would respond strongly enough to provoke a U.S.-China or China-Taiwan crisis, while another 31% expected a more limited negative response. Only two of the 64 experts believed formally committing America to Taiwan’s defense would actually deter China from using force because Beijing already assumes that the United States will intervene anyway.
A direct invasion is not even the most likely path toward conflict. Only 8% of the experts described an amphibious invasion within ten years as likely, while 63% called it possible and 27% unlikely. Force short of invasion received much higher probabilities, with 52% saying deliberate escalation such as a blockade was likely or very likely. An accidental military incident was considered even more dangerous, with 34% saying a collision or accident around the Taiwan Strait was likely and another 22% calling it very likely. When warships and aircraft from opposing nuclear powers continually operate around the same small body of water, war does not require some grand master plan. It requires one mistake followed by politicians who refuse to back down.
A later CSIS survey of American and Taiwanese experts reinforces that point. Roughly 90% of U.S. experts and 62% of Taiwanese experts believed China already possessed the capability to impose a law-enforcement-led quarantine that substantially reduces trade into Taiwan. Around 80% of American experts and 60% of Taiwanese experts believed Beijing could execute a PLA blockade, while Taiwanese experts were considerably more skeptical that China could successfully carry out an invasion. If Beijing wanted to coerce Taiwan during the following five years, experts considered a quarantine the most likely option. If China decided it wanted immediate unification, however, approximately 80% regarded a highly kinetic joint blockade as likely or very likely.
This is where the economic consequences become enormous because Taiwan does not need to be invaded for the world economy to be thrown into chaos. A quarantine or blockade would immediately threaten shipping, insurance, semiconductor supply chains, electronics, automobiles, communications equipment, and virtually every modern industry dependent upon advanced chips. The later CSIS survey found most American and Taiwanese experts did not believe Taiwan could withstand a Chinese blockade for longer than three months without substantial U.S. intervention. Washington would then face the decision nobody wants to discuss honestly: accept China’s blockade or attempt to break it militarily and risk direct war between two nuclear powers.
Taiwan is also the world’s semiconductor pressure point. The island’s importance to advanced chip manufacturing means a serious blockade would not remain a regional event. Factories thousands of miles away could discover that a conflict they thought had nothing to do with them suddenly prevents them from obtaining critical components. Markets would begin repricing the risk immediately, shipping premiums would explode, companies would scramble for inventory, and governments would discover once again how fragile global supply chains have become. This is why capital will react long before politicians formally declare that a war has begun.
What I find particularly revealing in the later CSIS survey is the difference between American confidence and Taiwanese confidence in Washington. An astonishing 96% of American experts were completely or moderately confident that the United States would intervene militarily if China invaded Taiwan during the following five years. Taiwanese experts were less confident in American intervention and considerably less confident that U.S. allies would join the fight. It is always easier for people thousands of miles away to be certain about somebody else’s war.
This is precisely why Taiwan remains one of the critical geopolitical pressure points as we move toward 2029. The danger is not simply that China arbitrarily decides to invade. The greater danger is escalation, miscalculation, political promises that cannot be withdrawn, and Western policymakers convincing themselves that every additional provocation somehow produces deterrence. China has made its position on formal independence perfectly clear, and even the experts inside the Western foreign-policy establishment overwhelmingly acknowledge that Beijing would react with force if that line were crossed.
If Taiwan declares formal independence, 77% of the experts surveyed believed China would invade within six months. That is not a statistic policymakers should treat as another war-game scenario. It is a warning about what happens when politicians deliberately remove the ambiguity that has helped keep the peace.

title: 吴祚来：陈吉宁落马五个最重要的原因
summary: 作者臉書 2026-11-25 官方目前仅通报陈吉宁“涉嫌严重违纪违法”，正接受中央纪委国家监委审查调查，未公布任何具体指控或细节。 网上已有的重大原因分析，主要来自BBC、联合早报、中央社等媒体及学者解读，集中在政治人事、派系与反腐信号层面，而非已证实的经济或具体违纪事实。 一、二十一大人事布局与“接班人”清除（最核心原因） 陈吉宁被广泛视为中共二十一大“入常”热门人选，甚至一度被列入潜在接班梯队。上海市委书记长期以来是通往政治局常委会的重要跳板：从江泽民、朱镕基、吴邦国
content: 作者臉書  2026-11-25 官方目前仅通报陈吉宁“涉嫌严重违纪违法”，正接受中央纪委国家监委审查调查，未公布任何具体指控或细节。 网上已有的重大原因分析，主要来自BBC、联合早报、中央社等媒体及学者解读，集中在政治人事、派系与反腐信号层面，而非已证实的经济或具体违纪事实。 一、二十一大人事布局与“接班人”清除（最核心原因） 陈吉宁被广泛视为中共二十一大“入常”热门人选，甚至一度被列入潜在接班梯队。上海市委书记长期以来是通往政治局常委会的重要跳板：从江泽民、朱镕基、吴邦国、黄菊，到习近平、俞正声、韩正、李强，几乎都是此路径。陈良宇2006年落马是唯一例外，之后四任全部入常。距离二十一大换届不到一年，陈吉宁在五中全会后仅六天仍公开调研（11月19日调研中远海运），突然落马，直接打断这一惯例，并牵动常委布局。 台湾政治大学寇健文等学者分析，这影响二十一大人事安排。有观点认为，习近平可能不打算设立明确接班人，或通过清除“潜在接班人”巩固权力。外媒曾盘点多个“习接班人”人选，已有多人出局或落马。陈吉宁的落马让下一届政治局更像“补缺”（补可靠的人）而非布局接班梯队。接任人选可能从外地大省调派、由现有副国级领导兼任，或让更年轻干部上位，但目前尚无定论。这是网上讨论最集中的重大原因。 二、“清华系”失势与陈希网络的最高级别打击 陈吉宁仕途与前中组部部长陈希（习近平清华同窗）关系密切。两人曾在清华共事，陈吉宁从环境系主任到副校长、校长的关键跃升，以及后来出任环保部长、北京市长、上海市委书记，多发生在陈希执掌中组部期间。外界普遍将其视为“清华系”（陈希长期经营提拔的旧部网络）核心成员。过去两年，该网络多人落马或边缘化：中组部系统旧部张建春、曹兴信被查；清华相关人士张尧学、魏小东、夏林茂等出事；李干杰与石泰峰职务对调、王希勤去职等信号，被解读为“去陈希化”。陈希本人2026年6月卸任中央党校校长等职后，有海外传闻称其被边缘化或软禁（未官方证实）。陈吉宁成为该网络级别最高的落马者，被BBC等称为“清华系失势”的标志性事件。若案件涉及干部任用或拉帮结派，可能进一步冲击该网络；若仅个人问题，则影响有限。这是派系层面最重大的分析。 三、高压反腐常态化与五中全会后的政治信号 二十届政治局已有四人落马（此前为何卫东、张又侠、马兴瑞），在改革开放以来罕见。刚刚闭幕的五中全会通过“推进全面从严治党”相关决定，被观察人士视为习近平将“常态化高压反腐”确立为长期治理模式的延续。陈吉宁落马时点敏感，上海市委常委会当晚扩大会议表态“坚决拥护”，并称这释放了“打赢反腐败斗争攻坚战持久战总体战的强烈信号”。网上解读认为，这显示无人能免（即使是形象清新的技术官僚、政治新星），反腐与“自我革命”不会松懈。具体违纪可能涉及经济问题、利益输送或干部选拔，但官方未披露，更多被看作政治信号而非单纯个案。 四、多重派系标签叠加与潜在具体问题（北京/上海任内） 陈吉宁身上叠加“清华系”（陈希）、“福建帮”关联（任北京市长时与时任市委书记蔡奇搭档近五年）以及主政上海后的“新老上海帮”色彩。网上有分析指，其落马可能与陈希推荐、干部任用问题，或上海/北京任内某些政商网络有关。有未证实传闻称，五中全会闭幕当天（10月29日）他曾被中央办公厅“叫走”谈话，可能涉及人事或陈希相关事宜，但其后仍公开活动至11月19日。问题究竟发生在上海、北京，还是更早阶段，有待调查。寇健文等指出，若牵涉政治立场、利益输送或干部任用，冲击会大于单纯个人经济问题。这是网上对“具体原因”的主要推测方向，目前缺乏公开证据。 五、打破“上海跳板”传统与地方一把手风险 这是时隔20年再有上海“一把手”任上被查（上次为陈良宇社保案）。传统上，上海书记被视为通往最高层的跳板，陈吉宁落马打破了陈良宇之后连续入常的纪录。网上解读认为，这折射干部考核机制可能存在漏洞，或高层对地方一把手（尤其是经济重镇）的控制加强。上海作为金融、航运中心及涉台交流重点地区，其书记落马也引发对后续政策连续性（如双城论坛等）的关注，但官方已表示继续支持相关交流。这与前述人事布局原因高度重叠，但强调地方权力与惯例被打破的一面。 总结：网上已有的重大原因几乎全部指向政治人事与派系博弈，而非已公开的具体腐败细节。官方通报极简，后续调查可能牵连更多人，或澄清为个人问题。这些分析基于公开履历、时点、派系关联与历史惯例，具有较强参考性，但目前仍属观察与推测。接任人选与案件具体走向，将成为观察二十一大布局的关键。

content:
JULIAN E. BARNES2026年11月26日
2024年台湾总统选举期间，台北的投票点。台湾将于11月28日举行地方选举。 Lam Yik Fei for The New York Times
研究人员发现，一场由人工智能驱动的协同社交媒体行动似乎正试图影响台湾本月的选举。
据信由与中国政府立场一致的团体控制的虚假账号正在推送支持中国共产党政策与立场的信息。
美国前官员和专家表示，中国的信息战行动传统上较为简陋。但这项研究表明，中国已利用人工智能——并可能借鉴了俄罗斯的做法——来改进其手段。
台湾将于11月28日举行地方选举，选出全岛各县市11000多个公职人员。中国将实行自治民主制度的台湾视为其领土的一部分。
台湾民事情报机构“国家安全局”已就中国干预此次选举发出警告。台湾官员本月也向Meta标记了数千个账号，称这些账号与中国有关联且参与了此次行动。
研究报告显示，10月和11月，范德堡大学的研究人员观察到旨在影响投票的“传统、混合以及人工智能驱动的非真实活动”。
去年，范德堡大学的研究人员发现，中国企业中科天玑正试图开发人工智能工具，以制造复杂的虚假信息行动。研究人员与台湾非营利组织台湾民主实验室合作，开始寻找中国不断扩大的人工智能驱动影响力行动的证据。
这项研究使用范德堡大学实验室开发的一种新工具，检测英文和中文的人工智能生成帖文及其他非真实内容。
范德堡大学国家安全研究所棘手问题实验室主任布雷特·J·戈德斯坦表示，研究团队“开发了识别人类与人工智能操作者在语气和用词偏好上细微差异的方法”。“这使我们能够在看似互不关联、却都在兜售政治叙事的账号之间识别出规律。”
该工具和研究人员发现，与北京立场一致的非真实账号要么发布美食、动物或名人等非政治话题，要么创建包含性感挑逗图像的社交媒体动态，即所谓的“诱惑陷阱”。在这些原本以娱乐为主的动态中，穿插着支持中国或统一的信息。
部分账号发布内容直接攻击台湾执政党民进党，指责其腐败或批评其施政表现。
还有一些虚假账号则采取了更为老练的手法。范德堡大学研究人员发现，有一个账号将自己包装成支持执政党的形象，却会回复那些未能引起关注的亲中账号，以使北京方面的信息获得更多关注。
研究发现，跨平台的账号在信息发布上相互协调，且似乎正在测试不同的策略。
中国驻美大使馆和台湾驻华盛顿代表处的发言人均未回应置评请求。
在无关的、以名人为中心的动态中植入政治信息的手法，在美国中期选举期间也曾被观察到。威胁情报公司Alethea认定，那些旨在削弱民主党人的虚假账号源自俄罗斯。
范德堡大学的研究显示，一些账号花了数月时间在Instagram上发布挑逗性的人工智能生成图像，随后在台湾选举临近之际，在配套社交媒体平台Threads上加入了政治内容。
范德堡大学政治学教授布雷特·本森表示，台湾此次出现的新型虚假信息行动展现出了惊人的耐心。
“合成虚拟人设有时会花数月时间发布非政治内容，积累粉丝并建立看似真实的社交媒体形象，然后再引入政治信息，”本森说。“人工智能正使构建和维护合成身份变得更加容易，这些身份在被用于政治目的之前，就能在社交网络中建立起可信度。”
该研究追踪的许多账号似乎是所谓的“赛博格”账号，即将人工智能生成的图像或口号与人类宣传人员的工作相结合。部分账号在正常办公时间发帖，表明有人参与操作，并非纯粹自动化运作。
范德堡大学此前针对中科天玑的研究显示，该公司曾试图利用人工智能制造超精准定向信息，希望根据人们的具体观点撰写大量信息以说服受众。
范德堡大学的这一新项目尚未发现此类超精准定向行动的证据，但研究人员表示他们仍在继续寻找。

title: SYS010 malware abuses browser management to spy on Gmail, Outlook
zh_title: SYS010 恶意软件滥用浏览器管理来监视 Gmail、Outlook
summary: SYS010 恶意软件滥用浏览器管理来监视 Gmail、Outlook SYS010 恶意软件滥用浏览器管理来监视 Gmail、Outlook SYS010 恶意软件滥用浏览器管理来监视 Gmail、Outlook 通过元广告传播的 SYS01 infostealer 恶意软件的新版本正在将浏览器注册到企业式管理中，以强制安装窃取敏感数据（包括 Gmail 和 Outlook 电子邮件）的扩展程序。这些广告引诱 Windows 用户下载免费的动画壁纸，这些壁纸的效果与广告中的一样，但在安装过程中也会在后台部署恶意软件。竞选活动
content:
SYS010 恶意软件滥用浏览器管理来监视 Gmail、Outlook
SYS010 恶意软件滥用浏览器管理来监视 Gmail、Outlook
SYS010 恶意软件滥用浏览器管理来监视 Gmail、Outlook
通过元广告传播的新版本 SYS01 infostealer 恶意软件正在将浏览器注册到企业式管理中，以强制安装窃取敏感数据（包括 Gmail 和 Outlook 电子邮件）的扩展程序。
这些广告引诱 Windows 用户下载免费的动画壁纸，这些壁纸的效果与广告中的一样，但在安装过程中也会在后台部署恶意软件。
该活动针对 Facebook 和 Meta 企业帐户，让运营商能够在 Chrome 中访问最近的 Gmail 和 Outlook 消息，并能够永久删除电子邮件。
Bitdefender Labs 将该活动追踪为 SYS010，并表示该恶意软件很可能是 SYS01 信息窃取程序的新版本，至少从 2022 年起就在 Facebook 的恶意广告活动中观察到该恶意软件。
该名称反映了研究人员的评估，即该变体比其前身有重大改进，因此他们将其标记为版本 2，以二进制表示为 010。
研究人员于 10 月 16 日发现了恶意 SYS010 广告，并发现该活动仍在进行中，已创建了数百个广告。
公司遥测显示，对威胁参与者服务器的请求来自亚洲、欧洲、北美、非洲和南美的多个国家。
Meta Ad Library 的透明度页面显示，仅一则广告就在欧盟覆盖了 6,275 名用户，目标人群为 18 岁以上的任何人。
SYS010 恶意广告中针对欧盟受众的元透明度页面
Bitdefender 在今天的一份报告中表示，大多数请求来自菲律宾、泰国、孟加拉国、波兰、墨西哥、阿尔及利亚、比利时、蒙古和美国，但强调这些数字并不反映已确诊的感染情况。
工作壁纸安装盗贼插件
这些广告冒充合法的壁纸引擎（基于 Electron 构建的 MeisterTask 桌面应用程序的重命名、数字签名版本）和 Lively 壁纸应用程序，将用户引导至恶意下载网站，其中一些网站使用看似官方的域名。
安装恶意 Windows 应用程序后，用户可以获得广告中宣传的动画壁纸功能，这有助于伪装在后台运行的恶意软件。
据 Bitdefender 研究人员称，攻击者通过滥用为组织设计的管理工具，迫使 Chrome、Edge 和 Firefox 安装恶意浏览器插件。
名为 eclient.php 的脚本负责通过修改浏览器管理策略来安装恶意扩展。
攻击者用于安装恶意浏览器扩展的 PHP 脚本
在 Chrome 中，它会将浏览器注册到攻击者控制的 Google 管理控制台中，从而允许强制安装扩展程序。
在 Firefox 中，它使用 ExtensionSettings 策略强制安装附加组件，同时禁用开发人员工具和滥用报告。
对于 Edge，它可以将受害者的 Windows 设备注册到攻击者控制的移动设备管理 (MDM) 服务器中，以启用强制扩展安装。
这些更改需要管理员权限，可以通过触发用户帐户控制 (UAC) 提示并每三秒重复一次最多 99 次直到用户批准该操作来解决。
Bitdefender 表示，这些控件可防止用户禁用或删除附加组件。然后，扩展程序可以窃取会话 cookie，从而允许恶意软件操作者访问 si

【原文 English Original】
SYS010 malware abuses browser management to spy on Gmail, Outlook
SYS010 malware abuses browser management to spy on Gmail, Outlook
SYS010 malware abuses browser management to spy on Gmail, Outlook
A new version of the SYS01 infostealer malware delivered through Meta ads is enrolling browsers into enterprise-style management to force the installation of an extension that steals sensitive data, including Gmail and Outlook emails.
The ads lure Windows users into downloading free animated wallpapers that work as advertised but also deploy malware in the background during installation.
The campaign targets Facebook and Meta business accounts and gives the operator access to recent Gmail and Outlook messages in Chrome, and the ability to permanently delete emails.
Bitdefender Labs tracks the campaign as SYS010 and says the malware is likely a new version of the SYS01 infostealer, observed since at least 2022 in malvertising activity on Facebook.
The name reflects the researchers' assessment that this variant represents a major improvement over its predecessor, leading them to tag it as version 2, represented in binary as 010.
Researchers identified a malicious SYS010 ad on October 16 and found that the campaign was still ongoing, with hundreds of ads created.
Company telemetry shows that requests to the threat actor’s servers came from several countries in Asia, Europe, North America, Africa, and South America.
Meta Ad Library' transparency page shows that one advertisement alone reached 6,275 users in the European Union, targeting anyone above 18.
Meta transparency page for EU audience in SYS010 malvertising
In a report today, Bitdefender says most requests came from the Philippines, Thailand, Bangladesh, Poland, Mexico, Algeria, Belgium, Mongolia, and the United States, but emphasizes these figures do not reflect confirmed infections.
Working wallpaper installs thieving add-on
The ads impersonate the legitimate Wallpaper Engine (a renamed, digitally signed version of the MeisterTask desktop app built on Electron) and Lively Wallpapers applications, directing users to malicious download sites, some of them using domains designed to appear official.
After installing the malicious Windows app, users get the advertised animated wallpaper functionality, which helps disguise the malware running in the background.
According to Bitdefender researchers, the attacker forces Chrome, Edge, and Firefox to install malicious browser add-ons by abusing management tools designed for organizations.
A script named eclient.php is responsible for installing the malicious extensions by modifying browser management policies.
Attacker PHP script for installing malicious browser extension
In Chrome, it enrolls the browser in an attacker-controlled Google admin console, allowing forced installation of extensions.
In Firefox, it uses an ExtensionSettings policy to force-install an add-on while disabling Developer Tools and abuse reporting.
For Edge, it can enroll the victim's Windows device in an attacker-controlled mobile device management (MDM) server to enable forced extension installation.
These changes require administrator permissions, which is solved by triggering the User Account Control (UAC) prompt and repeating it every three seconds up to 99 times until the user approves the action.
The controls prevent users from disabling or removing the add-ons, Bitdefender says. The extensions can then steal session cookies, allowing the malware operator to access signed-in accounts without entering passwords or completing a two-factor authentication challenge.
Bitdefender determined that the malicious add-ons pose as document tools, Docs Helper in Chrome and Document Hub in Firefox.
They note that the fake Docs Helper extension for Chrome uses an icon resembling the Google Docs logo but is distributed outside the Chrome Web Store.
The extensions also collect information about Facebook Pages, advertising and business accounts that the victim can access, including spending and payment details.
Bitdefender’s research also notes that the Chrome extension can read recent messages in Gmail and Outlook accounts and send their content to the attacker, as well as permanently delete selected messages.
This capability could let attackers intercept login codes and erase security alerts before victims see them, Bitdefender warns.
Furthermore, access to the same inbox could also make it harder to recover compromised accounts.
Similar behavior has been observed recently in another infostealer named Remus, which also uses a malicious extension to read messages in Gmail inboxes.
Remus infostealer takes a different approach to installing the extension in Chrome: it registers the add-on directly in the victim's browser profile and enables Developer Mode to allow the unpacked extension to run.
Although malvertising is often considered a lesser risk, it can still cause significant damage, as stolen advertising accounts are typically used to fund malvertising campaigns under the identity of trusted businesses.
Affected companies incur unauthorized advertising charges, and may lose access to their social media accounts, and have customer conversations exposed.
Bitdefender’s recommendation is to avoid downloading software from social-media ads and to refuse administrator prompts with an unclear purpose.
Additionally, an unexpected "managed by your organization" message in a browser should be a red flag. Individuals using a work-managed device should check with their IT team, while such a message on a personal computer warrants further investigation.
The cybersecurity company advises businesses to review who has access to their Meta accounts, remove permissions that are no longer needed, and check for unfamiliar ads, payment changes, or spending.

title: Public trial fascination shows open justice in action, says senior barrister
zh_title: 高级大律师表示，公开审判的魅力表明公开正义在行动
summary: 高级大律师表示，公开审判的魅力表明公开司法的实际行动中国劳工公告牌 星期五, 2026 年 11 月 27 日 · 香港 香港和中国劳工英文新闻 资深大律师 Victor Dawes SC 表示，公开审判的魅力表明了公开司法的实际行动，他认为公众​​对蔡艾比谋杀案审判的强烈兴趣体现了公开司法，这是香港法治的基石。他说，亲眼目睹诉讼程序有助于公众理解司法判决，区分理解与单纯的分歧。 2026 年 11 月 27 日 00:05 香港时间 · 更新于 11 月 27 日 04:27 · 2
content:
高级大律师表示，公开审判的魅力表明公开司法的实际行动中国劳工公告栏
星期五, 27 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
高级大律师表示，公开审判的魅力表明公开正义在行动
资深大律师维克多·道斯 (Victor Dawes) 认为，公众对蔡艾比谋杀案的强烈兴趣体现了公开司法，这是香港法治的基石。他说，亲眼目睹诉讼程序有助于公众理解司法判决，区分理解与单纯的分歧。
2026 年 11 月 27 日，香港时间 00:05 · 更新于 11 月 27 日，04:27 · 阅读时间 2 分钟
香港一位资深大律师表示，公众对最近的蔡碧儿谋杀案的强烈关注是公开司法的鲜明例证，而公开司法是法治的基本基础。
Victor Dawes SC 在《The Standard》中撰文指出，司法机构设立了人满为患的法庭，并进行现场直播以容纳人群，据报道，有数百人从早上 6 点开始排队等待上午 9 点 30 分的庭审。他将这种魅力比作福尔摩斯来到香港侦破最后一个案件，每个人都想在陪审团退席之前拼凑线索并做出裁决。
香港大律师公会前主席、现任香港国际仲裁中心联席主席道斯强调，刑事审判不是侦探小说，法庭也不是剧院。他写道，公开听证会不是为了娱乐，而是为了确保正义得到公开执行。公众应该能够看到证据是如何检验的、证人是如何盘问的以及司法判决是如何达成的。
他认为，当司法机构受到公众批评时，这一点尤其重要。人们常常根据头条新闻而不是其背后的证据和推理来判断司法判决。一份报纸报道无论写得多么好，都很少能传达全貌或捕捉到盘问的每一个细微差别或法官对证据的评估。亲眼目睹诉讼程序很可能是理解判决和不同意判决之间的区别。
道斯援引《基本法》第八十七条和《香港人权法案条例》第十条保护公平和公开听证的权利，称它们不仅仅是形式，而是法治的基石。他引用阿特金勋爵的话说：“正义不是一种与世隔绝的美德”；公众可以发挥基本作用——不是做出判决，而是确保正义永远不会成为“密室之谜”。
