title: Cyclic Materials picks Germany for first European plant
zh_title: 循环材料公司选择德国作为第一家欧洲工厂
summary: 稀土回收商 Cyclic Materials 在德国选择了一个地点作为其首个欧洲磁体回收设施，这标志着其国际扩张的一个里程碑。这家私营公司周四表示，在莱比锡附近施科保的陶氏价值园签署了一项设施土地预留协议。拟建工厂将为欧洲稀土回收网络奠定基础，有可能满足欧盟多达 15% 的稀土需求。 “欧洲知道可以通过国内循环稀土和关键矿产经济来实现经济弹性
content:
稀土回收商 Cyclic Materials 在德国选择了一个地点作为其首个欧洲磁体回收设施，这标志着其国际扩张的一个里程碑。这家私营公司周四表示，在莱比锡附近施科保的陶氏价值园签署了一项设施土地预留协议。拟建工厂将为欧洲稀土回收网络奠定基础，有可能满足欧盟多达 15% 的稀土需求。 Cyclic 首席执行官 Ahmad Ghahreman 在声明中表示：“欧洲知道通过国内循环稀土和关键矿产经济可以带来经济弹性。”这一扩张正值欧洲对稀土磁体的需求预计在未来十年内将增加一倍以上，而中国占全球加工稀土的 90%。回收可以帮助欧盟实现汽车、技术和国防工业必需材料的供应多元化，而无需开发新矿山。在微软（纳斯达克股票代码：MSFT）、亚马逊（纳斯达克股票代码：AMZN）和宝马（法国股票代码：BMW）等投资者的支持下，Cyclic 计划在德国工厂每年处理 25,000 吨磁力轴承废料。该工厂将为中央化学加工中心提供原料，回收的磁铁材料将在其中精炼并分离成稀土氧化物。 Ghahreman 告诉路透社，这家德国工厂是计划在欧洲建立的五个工厂中的第一个，预计于 2028 年开始运营。
该公司还在探索向中国以外的亚洲市场扩张。经过 17 个月的开发，Cyclic 于 9 月在亚利桑那州梅萨开设了第一家商业规模的磁体回收设施。该公司还在南卡罗来纳州建设一个综合回收园区。成本优势 Schkopau 工厂将使用 Cyclic 专有的 MagCycle 技术从废弃的电动机、硬盘、无人机和工业设备中提取永磁体。年产量可达 750 吨磁精矿、14,000 吨钢、4,600 吨铝和 3,000 吨铜。实地考察：Cyclic Materials 在亚利桑那州开设商业规模的稀土回收工厂 据路透社报道，额外金属的回收支撑了 Cyclic 的成本竞争力，非稀土材料占收入的 40% 至 50%。与 MP Materials（纽约证券交易所股票代码：MP）等已获得美国政府最低价格保证的生产商不同，Cyclic 表示，其生产成本使其无需类似支持即可运营。该公司还与电子产品回收商 ERI 合作，通过其美国收集网络确保原料安全，而其 REEPure 技术则在 10 月份登上《时代》杂志 2026 年最佳发明排行榜。当被问及潜在的首次公开募股时，Ghahreman 告诉路透社，Cyclic 此前已筹集 7500 万美元用于扩大其美国业务，并有多种筹集额外资金的选择。

【原文 English Original】
Rare earth recycler Cyclic Materials has selected a site in Germany for its first European magnet recovery facility, marking a milestone in its international expansion. The privately held company signed a land reservation agreement for a facility at the Dow ValuePark in Schkopau, near Leipzig, it said Thursday. The proposed plant would lay the groundwork for a European rare earth recovery network with the potential to meet as much as 15% of the EU’s rare earth needs. “Europe knows the economic resilience that can be delivered through a domestic, circular rare earth and critical mineral economy,” Cyclic CEO Ahmad Ghahreman said in the statement. The expansion comes as European demand for rare earth magnets is projected to more than double over the next decade, while China accounts for 90% of global processed rare earths. Recycling could help the European Union diversify its supplies of materials essential to the automotive, technology and defence industries without developing new mines. Backed by investors including Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) and BMW (FRA: BMW), Cyclic plans to process 25,000 tonnes of magnet-bearing scrap annually at the German facility. The plant would feed a central chemical processing hub, where recovered magnet material would be refined and separated into rare earth oxides. The German facility, the first of five planned for Europe, is slated to begin operations in 2028, Ghahreman told Reuters. The company is also exploring expansion into Asian markets outside China. Cyclic opened its first commercial-scale magnet recovery facility in Mesa, Arizona, in September following 17 months of development. It is also building an integrated recycling campus in South Carolina . Cost advantage The Schkopau plant would use Cyclic’s proprietary MagCycle technology to extract permanent magnets from discarded electric motors, hard drives, drones and industrial equipment. Annual output could reach 750 tonnes of magnet concentrate, alongside 14,000 tonnes of steel, 4,600 tonnes of aluminum and 3,000 tonnes of copper. Site visit: Cyclic Materials opens commercial-scale rare earth recycling plant in Arizona The recovery of additional metals underpins Cyclic’s cost competitiveness, with non-rare earth materials accounting for 40% to 50% of revenue, according to Reuters. Unlike producers such as MP Materials (NYSE: MP), which has secured minimum price guarantees from the US government, Cyclic says its production costs allow it to operate without similar support. The company has also partnered with electronics recycler ERI to secure feedstock through its US collection network, while its REEPure technology earned a spot on TIME’s Best Inventions of 2026 list in October. Cyclic previously secured $75 million to expand its US operations and has several options for raising additional capital, Ghahreman told Reuters when asked about a potential initial public offering.

title: China’s Cargo Drones Keep Getting Bigger With New W8000
zh_title: 新型 W8000 助力中国货运无人机不断发展壮大
summary: 中国部署越来越大的无人货运飞机的野心正在不断增强，白鲸航空推出了 W8000 货运无人机，据报道，这款货运无人机设计可承载 8 吨（略低于 18,000 磅）。该飞机代表了该公司自主货运航空计划的重大扩展，恰逢其较小的 W5000 已开始飞行测试。参观者在珠海 W8000 前合影。来自中国互联网 W5000（左）停在珠海的 W8000 旁边。来自中国互联网 W8000先于中国国际航空展亮相珠海
content:
中国部署越来越大的无人货运飞机的野心正在不断增强，白鲸航空推出了 W8000 货运无人机，据报道，这款货运无人机设计可承载 8 吨（略低于 18,000 磅）。该飞机代表了该公司自主货运航空计划的重大扩展，恰逢其较小的 W5000 已开始飞行测试。参观者在珠海 W8000 前合影。来自中国互联网 W5000（左）停在珠海的 W8000 旁边。来自中国互联网 W8000 在中国国际航空航天博览会（俗称中国航展）之前亮相珠海。在 12 月 7 日该活动开幕之前，我们已经抢先了解了一个平台，该平台旨在将无人货运能力提升到目前仅限于传统载人运输机的水平。据报道，其有效载荷为 8 吨，远高于 W5000，后者的设计载荷可达 5 吨（11,000 磅）。与 W5000 一样，W8000 可以通过后坡道装卸。 W8000 尾部的翻盖式门和后装载坡道。然而目前，双涡轮螺旋桨飞机 W8000 仍然是一个开发概念。其有效载荷数字只是设计目标，其航程、最大起飞重量和操作要求等细节仍不清楚。
为了进行比较，八吨的有效载荷将使 W8000 与 DHC-5 Buffalo 双引擎涡轮螺旋桨短距起降运输机处于同一类别。无论如何，此次亮相凸显了白鲸航空开发一系列大型无人驾驶货运飞机的雄心，目标是区域货运、偏远地区物流和潜在的军事运输任务，在这些任务中，自主飞机可以比传统货运业务提供优势。珠海W8000的后视图。来自中国互联网 双涡轮螺旋桨飞机 W8000 动力装置所使用的发动机尚未确定。通过中国互联网 更大的无人运输 W8000 的有效负载能力将使其能够运输大型设备、托盘货物、工业用品和其他大件货物。在商业环境中，大型自主货运飞机在公路或铁路基础设施有限或传统航空运输过于昂贵而无法频繁运营的航线上特别有用。尽管消除了机上机组人员，但飞机仍然需要维护人员、地勤人员、货物装载基础设施和支持性运营网络。最终，该飞机也可能被批准在受控空域内运行，取代载人支线货运业务，但这种用例在未来仍有一段路要走。不可避免的是，该飞机的发展也表明了大型货运无人机的潜在军事意义。
珠海的 W5000 和 W8000。来自中国互联网 W8000 可以为中国人民解放军 (PLA) 提供大量额外的空运选择，以保障在偏远、孤立或基础设施匮乏的地点作战的部队。这在印度-太平洋地区尤其重要，中国不断扩大的军事设施和岛屿前哨网络已经对频繁的补给飞行产生了需求。例如，在南中国海，大型货运无人机可以将设备、医疗用品、备件和其他必需品运输到远程设施，而无需载人运输

【原文 English Original】
China’s ambitions to field increasingly large, uncrewed cargo aircraft are growing, with Air White Whale unveiling its W8000, a cargo UAV reportedly designed to carry up to eight metric tons — a little less than 18,000 pounds. The aircraft represents a significant expansion of the company’s plans for autonomous freight aviation, coming just as its smaller W5000 has begun flight testing. Visitors pose in front of the W8000 at Zhuhai. via Chinese internet The W5000 (left) parked next to the W8000 at Zhuhai. via Chinese internet The W8000 appeared in Zhuhai, ahead of the China International Aviation & Aerospace Exhibition, commonly known as Airshow China . Before that event opens its doors on December 7, we have gotten an early look at a platform intended to push uncrewed cargo capacity into a class now limited to conventional, crewed transport aircraft. Its reported eight-ton payload would put it substantially above the W5000, which is designed to carry up to five metric tons (11,000 pounds). Like the W5000, the W8000 can be loaded and unloaded via a rear ramp. Clamshell doors and rear loading ramp in the tail of the W8000. via Chinese internet For now, however, the twin-turboprop W8000 remains a developmental concept. Its payload figure is a design target, and details about its range, maximum takeoff weight, and operational requirements are still unclear. For purposes of comparison, an eight-metric-ton payload would put the W8000 in much the same category as the DHC-5 Buffalo twin-engine turboprop STOL transport. Regardless, the unveiling highlights Air White Whale’s ambitions to develop a family of large uncrewed cargo aircraft, targeting regional freight, remote-area logistics, and potentially military transportation missions where autonomous aircraft could offer advantages over conventional cargo operations. Rear view of the W8000 at Zhuhai. via Chinese internet The engines used in the powerplant for the twin-turboprop W8000 are yet to be identified. via Chinese internet An Even Bigger Uncrewed Transport The W8000’s payload capacity would allow it to transport large equipment, palletized freight, industrial supplies, and other bulky cargo. In a commercial context, large autonomous cargo aircraft could be particularly useful on routes where road or rail infrastructure is limited, or where conventional air transport is too expensive to operate frequently. Although eliminating onboard flight crews, the aircraft would still require maintenance personnel, ground handling, cargo-loading infrastructure, and a supporting operational network. Ultimately, the aircraft could also be cleared to operate inside controlled airspace, displacing crewed feeder cargo operations, but that use case is still some way off in the future. Inevitably, the aircraft’s development also points toward the potential military relevance of large cargo UAVs. The W5000 and W8000 at Zhuhai. via Chinese internet The W8000 could offer the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) a substantial additional airlift option for sustaining forces operating from remote, isolated, or infrastructure-poor locations. This is particularly relevant in the Indo-Pacific, where China’s expanding network of military facilities and island outposts is already creating demand for frequent resupply flights. In the South China Sea, for example, large cargo UAVs could potentially transport equipment, medical supplies, spare parts, and other necessities to remote installations without requiring a crewed transport aircraft for every mission. They could also support operations in western China , including remote and high-altitude regions where road infrastructure is limited and conventional air transport can face additional challenges. There are also potential applications in a conflict, where conventional logistics infrastructure could be damaged or otherwise unavailable. Uncrewed transports would remove the risk to aircrews during routine resupply missions through contested airspace, although the aircraft themselves would remain vulnerable. They would also remove the need for combat search and rescue (CSAR) capabilities, which might be impossible to provide in at least some scenarios. Their usefulness would also depend, at least in some cases, on reliable communications, autonomous navigation, and the ability to operate without continuous access to satellite navigation. Profile view of the W8000 at Zhuhai. via Chinese internet W5000 Has Already Begun Flight Testing The W8000’s unveiling comes as Air White Whale’s smaller W5000 has reached a significant development milestone, completing its maiden flight on November 14. The five-ton cargo UAV reportedly conducted a roughly 30-minute test flight after taking off within approximately 600 meters (1,969 feet). During the flight, it reportedly conducted maneuvers and tested autonomous flight functions, datalink communications, propulsion, and flight-control systems before landing. China’s W5000 large cargo UAV has completed its maiden flight in the Ordos region of Inner Mongolia on 14 November. The aircraft reportedly took off after a 600 m (1,969 ft) ground run, climbed to 2,000 m (6,562 ft) and completed a 30-minute test flight. The trial included… pic.twitter.com/NNLqPKbLLZ — Drone Wars (@Drone_Wars_) November 14, 2026 The W5000 is designed to carry up to five metric tons of cargo, with a reported maximum range of 2,600 kilometers (1,616 miles), maximum takeoff weight of 10.8 tons (21,600 pounds), and cargo compartment volume exceeding 65 cubic meters (2,295 cubic feet). The aircraft is powered by twin turboprop engines. Chinese sources claim that Air White Whale has received 835 orders or prospective commitments from domestic logistics companies for the W5000, although the nature of those commitments and how many represent firm purchase contracts remain unclear. Commercial operations are currently planned to begin by the end of 2027, subject to further testing and certification. The W5000’s flight provides an indication of the company’s progress toward developing large uncrewed cargo aircraft, but the W8000 is a considerably more ambitious undertaking. Several other companies are also pursuing increasingly ambitious uncrewed transport aircraft. These include Tengden’s four-engine TB-001D Scorpion D , which first flew in October 2022 and is designed to carry up to 1.5 metric tons (3,307 pounds) of cargo, as well as the Star UAV System-developed AT200, another 1.5-ton-class cargo drone. The TB0D Scorpion D built by China’s Tengden Technology company completed its maiden flight in Sichuan on October 25, 2022. Twitter video screenshot Other designs include the state-owned Aviation Industry Corporation of China’s HH-100 , with a reported payload capacity of around 700 kilograms (1,543 pounds), and the China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation’s CH-YH1000 , designed to carry approximately one metric ton (2,205 pounds). While these aircraft vary considerably in size, configuration, and intended missions, their development highlights China’s broader push to establish uncrewed cargo aviation as a viable logistics capability. A demonstrator of China’s HH-100 commercial cargo drone. Photo by Yue Shuhua/VCG via Getty Images VCG Outside of China, there is some other notable activity in this sector. The United States is also pursuing large uncrewed cargo aircraft for military logistics. As we reported , Textron Aviation and autonomy specialist Merlin recently unveiled the Cessna SkyCourier UX, a concept based on the twin-engine Cessna 408 SkyCourier. The proposed aircraft would use Merlin’s autonomous flight system and could carry approximately 6,000 pounds of cargo. Its designers are exploring a cockpit-less configuration with a hydraulically opening nose section for direct cargo loading, as well as kneeling landing gear and integrated loading systems to simplify operations at austere locations. With a reported range of around 900 nautical miles, the SkyCourier UX is intended to support distributed military forces, including across the Pacific, where it could move supplies between larger logistics hubs and smaller, remote operating locations. The U.S. Air Force has also experimented with autonomous Cessna Caravan aircraft through Joby Aviation and its former Xwing autonomy team, including logistics demonstrations across the Pacific. Better known for land vehicles, Oshkosh Defense also recently announced a partnership with Silicon Valley startup Grid Aero, with the aim of building large military cargo drones. These would draw upon Grid Aero’s experience developing the Lifter family, an autonomous aircraft series with modular payload capacity that the company describes as a “pickup truck of the skies.” The Lifter is planned to carry somewhere between 1,000 and 8,000 pounds over a distance of approximately 1,500 miles.  The Grid Aero Lifter. Oshkosh/Grid Aero While the United States is moving slower than China in this space, there is arguably an even stronger operational case for such capabilities in the U.S. military, given the expeditionary nature of a potential conflict across the vast distances of the Indo-Pacific . Sustaining forces spread across widely separated islands, remote airfields, and austere forward operating locations would place enormous demands on conventional airlift and sealift networks. China Targets A New Class Of Cargo Aviation Overall, the development of the W5000 and W8000 highlights China’s growing interest in cargo UAVs capable of moving freight measured in metric tons rather than kilograms. While smaller delivery drones are increasingly being explored for last-mile transportation, aircraft such as the W8000 are aimed at moving substantial loads between logistics hubs without requiring an onboard crew. If the W8000 progresses, it could eventually offer a heavier transport option alongside the W5000, allowing Air White Whale to target different cargo requirements and routes. The W5000 and W8000 at Zhuhai ahead of Airshow China. via Chinese internet For now, the W8000 points to where Air White Whale wants to take its cargo UAV program. The W5000’s flight-test program will be an important step in establishing whether the company can turn its designs into operational aircraft and start to offer a new class of uncrewed airlift. Contact the author: thomas@thewarzone.com The post China’s Cargo Drones Keep Getting Bigger With New W8000 appeared first on TWZ .

title: 港府為外賣平台工作者提工傷保障立法 勞權監察批淪「次等勞工」變相被剝削
summary: 文章来源：追光者 作者：梁銘康 在香港從事外賣平台速遞等配送服務的「平台工作者」過去幾年多次發起罷工，爭取改善待遇及報酬。港府今年7月就加強平台工作者權益提出立法框架，但被指漏洞百出，包括未有設立工傷病假期間「每月最低收入」等。香港勞權監察發表報告，批評港府提出的框架將平台工作者界定為「次等勞工」，部分人所獲保障不進反退，警告若港府不正視問題，平台行業的勞資矛盾勢必越演越烈。 勞權監察周一（23日）發表題為《聊勝於無？香港政府建議為平台工作者設立的工傷補償機制》的報告，批評港
content: 文章来源：追光者 作者：梁銘康 在香港從事外賣平台速遞等配送服務的「平台工作者」過去幾年多次發起罷工，爭取改善待遇及報酬。港府今年7月就加強平台工作者權益提出立法框架，但被指漏洞百出，包括未有設立工傷病假期間「每月最低收入」等。香港勞權監察發表報告，批評港府提出的框架將平台工作者界定為「次等勞工」，部分人所獲保障不進反退，警告若港府不正視問題，平台行業的勞資矛盾勢必越演越烈。 勞權監察周一（23日）發表題為《聊勝於無？香港政府建議為平台工作者設立的工傷補償機制》的報告，批評港府的立法建議迴避平台工作者最核心的勞工權益問題，拒絕確立他們的僱員身份，更透過界定工作者資格、限制受保障的工作時段及壓低補償計算基礎等安排，層層收窄工傷保障範圍，令平台工作者最終只獲遠遜於一般僱員的次等保障。 報告批立法框架存在多個漏洞 報告指港府的立法框架存在若干明顯缺陷，包括等單、搶單期間受傷不受保障；兼職平台工作者若不幸因工受傷，其他非平台工作收入不計算在工傷補償以內；計算平台工作者在工傷病假期間的按期付款時，不設類似現行《僱員補償條例》下的「每月最低收入」規定 ；替工及經中介聘用的平台工作者更可能完全被拒諸門外。 有別於新加坡《2024年平台工作者法》（Platform Workers Act 2024） ，港府提出的立法框架完全無條文規定營運者，要採取措施保障平台工作者的安全及健康。勞權監察批評「只賠不防」在政策上說不通，強調工傷的補償與預防兩者密不可分。 質疑無異於變相剝削 勞權監察形容港府的立法框架，由界定工作者身份、工傷發生時間，到計算補償金額皆「處處設限」，不斷收窄營運者的責任，把平台工作者的保障壓低至遠遜於一般僱員的水平，變相剝削，令人質疑立法是為保障平台工作者，抑或為平台營運者卸責打開方便之門 。報告又指最低工資及監管平台演算法等其他勞工權益，完全無納入框架。一旦落實，平台工作者除了將被長期排除於基本勞工權益之外，遇上工傷時能否維持生活也成疑問。 報告提出多項補救建議，包括將工傷保障範圍，擴展至平台工作者登入其帳戶期間發生的意外；訂明「每月最低收入」適用於暫時喪失工作能力的按期付款等；提出將勞資審裁處的司法管轄權擴展至平台工作者等長期政策倡議。勞權監察總幹事蒙兆達指，縱然近年香港政治氣氛高壓下，仍爆發多宗 「 外賣車手」工潮，反映平台工作者的怨氣正日益加深，警告若港府不正視問題，平台行業的勞資矛盾只會越演越烈。

summary: 黄蜂级两栖攻击舰马金岛号 (LHD-8) 于 2026 年 10 月 26 日抵达日本横须贺舰队活动司令部。美国海军照片 两栖攻击舰马金岛号 (LHD-8) 和两栖运输船坞号 USS 约翰·P·默斯 a (LPD-26) 于周二从新加坡三巴旺出发，前往印度洋。根据当地船舶观察员和 AIS 数据，马金岛号和约翰·P·默塔号随第 13 海军陆战队远征部队的部队出发，正在通过马六甲海峡向北航行。 AIS数据显示两艘船当时位于马六甲以南的马六甲海峡
content:
黄蜂级两栖攻击舰马金岛号 (LHD-8) 于 2026 年 10 月 26 日抵达日本横须贺舰队活动司令部。美国海军照片 两栖攻击舰马金岛号 (LHD-8) 和两栖运输船坞号 USS 约翰·P·默斯 a (LPD-26) 于周二从新加坡三巴旺出发，前往印度洋。根据当地船舶观察员和 AIS 数据，马金岛号和约翰·P·默塔号随第 13 海军陆战队远征部队的部队出发，正在通过马六甲海峡向北航行。 AIS数据显示，两艘船于晚上10点位于马来西亚首都吉隆坡以南的马六甲海峡。当地时间，美国海军拉帕汉诺克号舰队加油船 (T-AO-204)。马金岛、约翰·P·穆萨、两栖运输船坞舰安克雷奇号 (LPD-23) 和已登船的第 13 远征远征队组成了马金岛两栖准备大队。安克雷奇及其第 13 海军陆战队远征部队分队目前驻扎在日本横须贺司令舰队活动司令部 (CFAY)。据 USNI News 此前报道，ARG 于 9 月 28 日从圣地亚哥出发。第13远征部队的海军陆战队空地特遣部队包括第13远征部队指挥分队、作为地面作战分队的第2/4营登陆队和作为其后勤分队的第13战斗后勤营。航空中队包括海军陆战队中型倾转旋翼机中队 (VMM) 364（增援）和海军陆战队战斗机攻击中队 (VMFA) 211，其中包括 MV-22B 鱼鹰、CH-53、AH-1Z 毒蛇和 F-35B 闪电 II。
ARG 于 10 月初驶入夏威夷进行港口访问，然后穿越太平洋。安克雷奇于 10 月 21 日至 22 日对关岛进行了短暂访问，然后重新加入 ARG，并于 10 月 26 日驶入 CFAY 进行港口访问。所有三艘 ARG 舰艇均于 11 月 7 日从 CFAY 出发，与约翰·P·穆萨号和安克雷奇号一起参加“马拉巴尔 2026”演习的海上阶段，这是澳大利亚、日本、印度和美国“四方”伙伴关系下的年度海军演习。演习于 11 月 5 日至 12 日在横须贺及其周边地区举行。印度海军什瓦里克级隐形多用途护卫舰INS Sahyadri (F 49)、日本海上自卫队日向级直升机驱逐舰JS Ise (DDH 182)、最上级护卫舰JS Mogami (FFM 1)、澳大利亚皇家海军安扎克级护卫舰HMAS Stuart (FFH 153)和美国海军圣安东尼奥级两栖运输舰2026 年马拉巴尔演习期间，美国海军安克雷奇号 (LPD-23) 和约翰·P·穆萨 (LPD-26) 号船坞编队在西太平洋航行，2026 年 11 月 7 日。美国海军照片 与约翰·P·穆萨和安克雷奇一起参加演习的有日本海上自卫队直升机驱逐舰 JS 伊势 (DDH-182)、护卫舰 JS 最上(FFM-1)、一艘日本海上自卫队潜艇、印度海军护卫舰 INS Sahyadri (F49)、澳大利亚皇家海军护卫舰 HMAS Stuart (FFH153)、一架美国海军 P-8A 海神海上巡逻机和一架日本海上自卫队 P-1 MPA。演习活动包括海军炮火、反水面战演习和反潜战演习。伊势和约翰·P.
穆萨号进行了互访、登船、搜查和扣押（VBSS）演习。“马拉巴尔2026”号完成后，约翰·P·穆萨号前往菲律宾海与马金岛会合。据当地船舶观察员称，“安克雷奇”号于 11 月 13 日在横须贺近海抛锚，并于 11 月 16 日停靠在 CFAY，占据了离开的潜艇母舰弗兰克·电缆号 (AS-40) 所腾出的空间。马金岛号和约翰·P·默撒号于周五穿越南中国海，抵达新加坡三巴旺进行港口访问。海军和五角大楼都没有表示安克雷奇是否会加入马

Murtha , amphibious transport dock USS Anchorage (LPD-23) and the embarked 13th MEU form the Makin Island Amphibious Ready Group. Anchorage and its embarked 13th MEU elements are currently at Commander Fleet Activities Yokosuka (CFAY), Japan. The ARG departed from San Diego on Sept. 28, USNI News previously reported . The 13th MEU’s Marine Air-Ground Task Force includes the 13th MEU command element, Battalion Landing Team 2/4 as the Ground Combat Element and Combat Logistics Battalion 13 as its logistic element. The aviation squadrons are Marine Medium Tiltrotor Squadron (VMM) 364 (Reinforced) and Marine Fighter Attack Squadron (VMFA) 211, which includes MV-22B Ospreys, CH-53s, AH-1Z Vipers and F-35B Lightning IIs. The ARG pulled into Hawaii for a port visit in early October before transiting the Pacific. Anchorage made a short visit to Guam from Oct. 21-22 before rejoining the ARG, which pulled into CFAY on Oct. 26 for a port visit. All three ARG ships departed Nov. 7 from CFAY with John P. Murtha and Anchorage participating in the sea phase of Exercise Malabar 2026, an annual naval exercise under the “Quad” partnership of Australia, Japan, India and the U.S. The exercise ran from Nov. 5-12 in and around Yokosuka. Indian Navy Shivalik-class stealth multi-role frigate INS Sahyadri (F 49), Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force Hyuga-class helicopter destroyer JS Ise (DDH 182), Mogami-class frigate JS Mogami (FFM 1), Royal Australian Navy Anzac-class frigate HMAS Stuart (FFH 153) and U.S. Navy San Antonio-class amphibious transport docks USS Anchorage (LPD-23) and USS John P. Murtha and Anchorage were Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force helicopter destroyer JS Ise (DDH-182), frigate JS Mogami (FFM-1), a JMSDF submarine, Indian Navy frigate INS Sahyadri (F49), Royal Australian Navy frigate HMAS Stuart (FFH153), a U.S. Navy P-8A Poseidon Maritime Patrol Aircraft and a JMSDF P-1 MPA. Exercise activities included naval gunfire, anti-surface warfare drills and anti-submarine warfare drills. Ise and John P. Murtha carried out reciprocal visit, board, search, and seizure (VBSS) drills . Following completion of Malabar 2026, John P. Murtha headed out to the Philippine Sea to join Makin Island . Anchorage anchored offshore at Yokosuka on Nov. 13 and docked into CFAY on Nov. 16, taking the space vacated by departing submarine tender USS Frank Cable (AS-40), according to local ship spotters . Makin Island and John P. Murtha transited the South China Sea and pulled into Sembawang, Singapore on Friday for a port visit. The Navy nor the Pentagon has said whether Anchorage will join Makin Island and John P. Murtha . Makin Island and John P. Murtha are heading towards the Indian Ocean. Makin Island and John P. Murtha are expected to relieve the Boxer ARG in the Middle East. The Boxer ARG, which includes amphibious assault ship USS Boxer (LHD-4), amphibious dock landing ship USS Comstock (LSD-45) and amphibious transport dock USS Portland (LPD-27) and the embarked 11th MEU, deployed out from the West Coast in March, USNI News reported , putting it at eight months deployed. Boxer and Comstock were operating in U.S. Central Command as of Monday while Portland was operating in U.S. 7th Fleet area of operations, according to the USNI News Fleet and Marine Tracker .

title: China’s Naval Developments Set For The Spotlight At Zhuhai Airshow
zh_title: 中国海军发展成为珠海航展的焦点
summary: 中国人民解放军海军表示，正在准备在即将于珠海举行的第十六届中国国际航空航天博览会上进行重要亮相，军舰、舰载机、先进武器系统和无人平台将成为重点展示。扩大后的海军部分将包括在海湾另一边的高栏港设立一个新的海事装备展区，这标志着解放军海军首次在此次活动中设立这样的专门展示区。珠海已成为国际防务、航空领域最重要的赛事之一
content:
中国人民解放军海军表示，正在准备在即将于珠海举行的第十六届中国国际航空航天博览会上进行重要亮相，军舰、舰载机、先进武器系统和无人平台将成为重点展示。扩大后的海军部分将包括在海湾另一边的高栏港设立一个新的海事装备展区，这标志着解放军海军首次在此次活动中设立这样的专门展示区。珠海已成为国际国防和航空航天史上最重要的活动之一，成为中国快速发展的航空和军事工业的主要公开展示地。两年一度的中国国际航空航天展览会（俗称中国航展）于 1996 年首次举办，为展示中国一些最先进的军事硬件提供了难得的机会，其中包括在其他地方很少如此详细展示的飞机和系统。虽然该活动也是中国航空航天工业向潜在国际客户推广其产品的主要平台，但它日益成为展示新军事能力和提供难以评估的项目的重要场所。
第十五届中国国际航空航天展览会（又称 2024 年中国航展）于 2024 年 11 月 15 日在中国广东省珠海市中国国际航空航天展览中心举行。摄影：VCG/VCG via Getty Images 前几届已经取得了一些特别重大的进展。 2016 年的展会上，J-20 隐形战斗机首次公开飞行亮相，而 2018 年的展会则以不同寻常的方式展示了这架飞机，包括展示其装载空对空导弹的内部武器舱。 2022年的展会上，歼20首次在珠海进行静态展示，同时还有运20重型运输机、直20直升机以及在展会上进行首次飞行演示的运20空中加油机。最近，2024 年的展会特别引人注目的是 J-35A 隐形战斗机的公开亮相和具有弹射能力的 J-15T 舰​​载战斗机的出现。一架 J-15T 舰​​载战斗机在 2024 年中国航展上进行飞行表演。CFOTO/Future Publishing via Getty Images 今年的展览定于 12 月 7 日至 13 日举行，除其他外，将展示中国海军的广泛能力，特别强调其舰载航空能力的快速发展，这一点我们过去已经详细讨论过。
预计将亮相的最引人注目的飞机包括 J-15T 舰载战斗机、作战型 J-35 隐形战斗机、KJ-600 舰载机载预警和控制 (AEW&C) 飞机、Z-20 直升机的几种海军型号，也许最重要的是新型 JL-15 舰载教练机，它是陆基 JL-10 的发展型。JL-15 舰载教练机的照片突出显示了制动钩和弹射器发射杆。虽然我们之前在珠海见过 J-15T，但如果它配备国产 WS-10H2 发动机，将会引起特别的兴趣。这样的配置将让人们更仔细地了解中国舰载侧卫衍生产品的最新演变

【原文 English Original】
China’s People’s Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) says it’s preparing a major presence at the upcoming 16th China International Aviation & Aerospace Exhibition in Zhuhai, with warships , carrier-based aircraft , advanced weapons systems, and uncrewed platforms set to feature prominently. The expanded naval component will include a new maritime equipment exhibition area at Gaolan Port, located just on the other side of the bay, marking the first time the PLAN has established such a dedicated display at the event. Zhuhai has become one of the most important events on the international defence and aerospace calendar, serving as China’s principal public showcase for its rapidly developing aviation and military industries. First held in 1996, the biennial China International Aviation & Aerospace Exhibition, commonly known as Airshow China, provides an unusual opportunity to see some of the country’s most advanced military hardware, including aircraft and systems that are rarely shown in such detail elsewhere. While the event also serves as a major platform for China’s aerospace industry to promote its products to potential international customers , it has increasingly become an important venue for revealing new military capabilities and offering glimpses of programs that are otherwise difficult to assess. A general view of the 15th China International Aviation & Aerospace Exhibition, or Airshow China 2024, at the China International Aviation & Aerospace Exhibition Center on November 15, 2024, in Zhuhai, Guangdong Province of China. Photo by VCG/VCG via Getty Images Previous editions have produced some particularly significant developments. The 2016 show saw the J-20 stealth fighter make its first public flying appearance , while the 2018 edition provided an unusually revealing look at the aircraft, including a demonstration of its internal weapons bays, loaded with air-to-air missiles . The 2022 exhibition featured the J-20 on static display for the first time at Zhuhai, alongside the Y-20 heavy transport aircraft, Z-20 helicopter, and YY-20 aerial refueling tanker, which made its first flying demonstration at the event. More recently, the 2024 exhibition was particularly notable for the public debut of the J-35A stealth fighter and the appearance of the catapult-capable J-15T carrier-based fighter. A J-15T carrier-based fighter conducts a flight demonstration at Airshow China 2024. CFOTO/Future Publishing via Getty Images This year’s exhibition, scheduled to take place from December 7 to 13, will showcase, among others, a broad range of the PLAN’s capabilities, with a particularly notable emphasis on the rapid evolution of its carrier aviation capabilities, something we have addressed in detail in the past . Among the most noteworthy aircraft expected to feature are the J-15T carrier-based fighter, the operational J-35 stealth fighter, the KJ-600 carrier-based airborne early warning and control (AEW&C) aircraft, several naval variants of the Z-20 helicopter, and, perhaps most significantly, the new JL-15 carrier-capable trainer, a development of the land-based JL-10 . A photo of the JL-15 carrier-capable trainer with the arrestor hook and catapult launch bar highlighted. Chinese internet via X While we have seen the J-15T at Zhuhai before, the aircraft will be of particular interest if it is shown with the indigenous WS-10H2 engine. Such a configuration would offer a closer look at the latest evolution of China’s carrier-based Flanker derivative and its ongoing transition toward a more domestically supported carrier aviation ecosystem. The appearance of the J-35 would be another major highlight. The aircraft represents a significant step in the PLAN’s carrier aviation ambitions, bringing a fifth-generation stealth fighter capability into the carrier air wing. Its presence would provide another opportunity to examine the progress of China’s next-generation naval fighter program. Back in 2014, Zhuhai saw the public debut of the FC-31 fighter demonstrator. At the time, it was still a land-based concept, and export was the main talking point, although there was already speculation about a naval variant, today’s J-35. A People’s Liberation Army Navy J-35 fighter during trials from the carrier Fujian last year. Chinese internet via X Meanwhile, the KJ-600 is arguably one of the most important developments in the PLAN’s carrier aviation ecosystem. The twin-engine turboprop aircraft is designed to provide airborne early warning and battle management capabilities, something that would transform the situational awareness and coordination available to China’s carrier strike groups. One of the first high-definition photos of the KJ-600 carrier-based airborne early warning and control (AEW&C) aircraft. Chinese internet via X Several variants of the Z-20 family are also expected to feature, reflecting the growing importance of helicopters in carrier operations, including airborne anti-submarine warfare, utility, and other maritime support missions. You can read more about the Z-20 family and other Chinese rotary-wing developments in this previous TWZ deep-dive on the topic . A Z-20F, the anti-submarine warfare variant of the naval Z-20 family. Three more naval Z-20s are seen in the hangar behind, including a Z-20J shipborne transport and assault variant. Chinese internet via X Perhaps the most intriguing aircraft on the list, however, is the JL-15. The JL-15 is derived from the Hongdu JL-10, also exported as the L-15 Falcon, a twin-engine advanced jet trainer and lead-in fighter trainer. The navalized development was initially reported to be designated JL-10J, but is now confirmed as being the JL-15. A tailhook-equipped mockup was spotted alongside the aircraft carrier Fujian in 2024. However, its operational status remains unclear, and China is known to have encountered difficulties with its earlier JL-9G naval trainer, whose tailhook was reportedly deleted following structural problems. Regarding the rumoured JL-10J carrier-capable jet trainer, another hint was spotted next to the carrier Fujian: It appears to be an unfinished JL-10J mockup stored on the dockside . So question is: Two tails as shown in the latest CG or just one like the regular JL-10? pic.twitter.com/BM8W8MRGWK — @Rupprecht_A (@RupprechtDeino) March 19, 2024 Its appearance would provide a particularly interesting indication of how China is thinking about training its next generation of carrier-based pilots. A carrier-capable development of the JL-10 would be an important addition to the emerging carrier aviation ecosystem, bridging the gap between conventional jet training and the demanding requirements of operating from an aircraft carrier. The JL-15 also makes an interesting comparison with the U.S. Navy’s somewhat stuttering efforts to introduce a new training jet for its carrier pilots. The U.S. Navy’s Undergraduate Jet Training System (UJTS) program is intended to replace its aging fleet of T-45 Goshawk trainers, but the acquisition effort has encountered considerable difficulties. Earlier this month, we described how Sierra Nevada Corporation (SNC) withdrew its proposed clean-sheet Freedom Jet from the competition, citing concerns over the Navy’s insistence on firm-fixed-price production commitments before the aircraft’s design had sufficiently matured. This leaves the Beechcraft M-346N , based on Leonardo’s established M-346 Master , as the only publicly known remaining contender . The program has also experienced schedule slippage, with the initial contract award now expected in the fourth quarter of Fiscal Year 2027. Perhaps more significant is the difference in the two services’ approaches to carrier aviation training. The U.S. Navy has removed the requirement for its next-generation jet trainer to be capable of operating from an actual aircraft carrier, including carrier qualification and simulated carrier touch-and-goes at land-based facilities. Instead, it increasingly relies on advanced simulation, virtualized training, and assisted carrier landing technologies to prepare pilots for the demands of carrier operations. The JL-15, by contrast, is intended to support carrier-based pilot training. A dedicated carrier-capable trainer could offer China a more direct pathway for preparing pilots for operations aboard its increasingly sophisticated — and expanding — carrier fleet. Taken together, the PLAN aircraft being lined up for Zhuhai this year illustrate the increasingly sophisticated and integrated nature of China’s carrier aviation ambitions . As well as the aircraft carriers and their embarked aircraft, these ambitions also require other surface and subsurface vessels to operate effectively. Uncrewed systems will form another important part of the display. The exhibition will include aerial drones, uncrewed underwater vehicles, and other autonomous platforms, reflecting the PLAN’s growing interest in the potential of uncrewed warfare. Chinese media reports suggest that the WZ-2 uncrewed helicopter will receive its public debut at Zhuhai, while the PLAN may well also want to capitalize on its recent announcement that it had successfully launched and recovered a GJ-21 stealthy flying-wing uncrewed combat air vehicle (UCAV) aboard the Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan . GJ-21. Chinese internet via X A chance to see the GJ-21 up close would be a huge deal, but there are many other naval drone options that could be revealed in more detail. There are likely to be more navalized collaborative combat aircraft (CCA) concepts and developments, especially since the adoption of the electromagnetic aircraft launch system (EMALS) catapult opens up a huge range of possibilities for uncrewed aircraft operating as part of a carrier air wing. Potentially, these could include the mysterious MQ-25-like drone that we recently discussed , the role of which remains unclear. On top of that, constant CCA testing at locations such as Malan suggests there could be much more to discuss than just the systems officially highlighted. Many other naval drones will surely be on display as well, including lower-end attritable concepts. Beyond static displays, China’s navy plans to organize flight demonstrations, formation flights, and simulated operational exercises. Its stated aim is to highlight not only the capabilities of individual platforms but also their ability to operate together in complex maritime environments. Photos have emerged showing apparent rehearsals for the display, presenting examples of the J-15, J-35, and KJ-600 to represent Beijing’s broader carrier air wing ecosystem. Two J-15s, two J-35s, and a KJ-600 purportedly taking part in a rehearsal for a formation fly-over at Zhuhai. Chinese internet via X It is not immediately clear which versions of the J-15 are participating in this formation flight: they could be J-15Ts, but another possibility is the electronic warfare version, the J-15DT , that we have profiled in the past. Regardless, they highlight how China’s carrier aviation ambitions are increasingly focused on catapult-assisted takeoff but arrested recovery (CATOBAR) operations, which offer many advantages . The J-15DT electronic warfare version of the Chinese carrier Flanker is outfitted for operations aboard catapult-equipped flattops like the Fujian . Chinese internet via X For the first time, the exhibition will also include a substantial surface fleet component, making use of the docks at the nearby Gaolan Port. Among the vessels expected to be featured are the Type 075 amphibious assault ship, the Type 055 guided-missile destroyer, and the Type 054A guided-missile frigate. Their presence will offer a public-facing showcase of China’s increasingly sophisticated surface fleet and its expanding range of maritime capabilities. It should also be recalled that it was at Gaolan Port where at least one Chinese uncrewed surface vessel , a distinctive trimaran craft, was first spotted. The Type 055 guided-missile destroyer Nanchang sails during the naval exercise Joint Sea-2021 on October 19, 2021, in the Western part of the Pacific Ocean. Photo by Sun Zifa/China News Service via Getty Images The broader messaging surrounding the exhibition is also notable. According to the PLAN, this year’s displays will place greater emphasis on operational readiness and training, with active-duty equipment that regularly participates in exercises and maritime security missions taking precedence over purely exhibition-oriented displays. This should underscore how Beijing has rapidly spun up its naval capabilities, introducing new and more capable equipment that is increasingly capable of more sustained out-of-area operations. The expanded naval presence at Zhuhai looks set to provide a substantial public showcase of China’s ongoing naval modernization. As well as the combination of the J-15T, J-35, KJ-600, and Z-20 variants, the JL-15 points to an increasingly comprehensive carrier aviation enterprise. And, judging by previous editions of the show, there will almost certainly be more novelties on display as well.
